signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-01 mobile-native-kmp realtor create-listing wiring)
evidence: mobile-native/androidApp/.../navigation/Navigation.kt:490-495 — the composable for Screen.CreateListing wires CreateListingScreen with `onSubmit = { _ -> Result.failure(NotImplementedError("Wire to listing API")) }`. This is the ONLY (production) wiring of the create-listing submit callback — not a test stub, not a preview.

The screen is a fully built, reachable feature: MyListingsScreen (Navigation.kt:480-488) exposes `onCreateClick = { navController.navigate(Screen.CreateListing.route) }`, and CreateListingScreen.kt:39-131 is a complete form (title/description/city/price/currency/transactionType) with field validation (titleError/cityError/priceError, CreateListingScreen.kt:96-104), an isSubmitting spinner (CreateListingScreen.kt:105-129, 375), and a real Result.fold handler.

Because onSubmit ALWAYS returns Result.failure, the fold at CreateListingScreen.kt:120-126 always takes the onFailure branch and renders `publishFailedMsg` ("publish failed") — or networkErrorMsg if it.isNetworkError(), which NotImplementedError is not. A realtor who fills the form and taps Publish is guaranteed to see a failure toast every time; the listing is never created.

Root cause: PortalListingsRepository (shared/.../realtor/PortalListingsRepository.kt) exposes only listMyListings (:40), getListingAnalytics (:74) and getPortfolioAnalytics (:111) — there is NO create/publish method to back the screen. The UI shipped ahead of the repository + API call.

Fix: add `suspend fun createListing(input: CreateListingInput): Result<Unit>` to PortalListingsRepository (POST to the reality-server realtor listings endpoint via ApiClient, wrapped in the same Result/onFailure convention as the other repo methods), then wire `onSubmit = { input -> portalListingsRepository.createListing(input) }` in Navigation.kt:493. Add a commonTest for the repository path encoding + success/failure mapping (mirrors PortalListingsRepositoryTest). Confidence high: full call path traced entry(MyListings onCreateClick) -> CreateListing route -> onSubmit -> NotImplementedError -> publishFailedMsg, reachable in the shipped android build; no runtime needed to confirm the callback is hardcoded to fail.

mobile-native/androidApp/.../navigation/Navigation.kt — four list-loading composables collapse a repository failure into an empty list with no error surface: SavedSearches `.onFailure { searches = emptyList() }` (:380), Inquiries `.onFailure { inquiries = emptyList() }` (:450), MyListings `.onFailure { listings = emptyList() }` (:476), and ListingAnalytics `.onFailure { metrics = emptyList() }` (:541).

In every case the child screen is then handed the same empty list it would receive when the account genuinely has no data, so a network/auth/5xx failure is rendered as the benign empty-state ('You have no listings yet' / 'No saved searches'). The user is told they have nothing when in fact the load failed, and there is no retry affordance — the LaunchedEffect only runs once per key, so a transient failure is sticky until the screen is left and re-entered.

This diverges from the pattern the rest of the app uses: ListingDetailScreen distinguishes state.errorMessage != null -> ErrorContent(onRetry = viewModel::retry) (ListingDetailScreen.kt:120-121), and CreateListingScreen shows a distinct networkError vs generic failure. The realtor/saved-search/inquiry list screens should do the same rather than masking failure as emptiness.

Fix: track a load-error flag alongside the list (e.g. `var loadError by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }`), set it in onFailure instead of overwriting the list, and have each *Screen render an error+retry state when it is set. Add commonTest / UI coverage asserting that a repository Result.failure yields an error state, not an empty list. Confidence medium: the swallow is confirmed by static read; the exact UX impact per screen depends on each *Screen's empty-state copy which was not exhaustively read.

mobile-native/androidApp/.../ui/listing/ListingDetailScreen.kt:131-139 — the onCallClick lambda dereferences `state.listing!!.realtor?.phone` with a non-null assertion. Unlike the sibling `!!` sites (L121 errorMessage, L125/149/160 listing) which are guarded by an immediately-enclosing `when { state.listing != null -> ... }` / `if (state.listing != null)` in the SAME scope (safe smart-cast, `!!` is only needed because Kotlin cannot smart-cast a delegated `by collectAsState()` property), onCallClick is a DEFERRED callback: it captures `state` and runs on a later user tap.

`state` is a `by collectAsState()` delegate, so `state.listing` is re-read from the current StateFlow value at click time. If the ViewModel emits a new state whose listing is null (e.g. a retry/reload transition, or an inquiry-submitted event that resets state) between the phone button becoming visible and the tap, `state.listing!!` throws NullPointerException and crashes the screen.

Likelihood is low (the button is only composed inside the listing != null branch, so state must flip null after render but before tap), which is why this is scored Low, but it is a genuine crash path rather than a smart-cast nicety.

Fix: capture the listing into a local val at composition and null-check it, or read `state.listing?.realtor?.phone?.let { ... }` inside the lambda instead of `state.listing!!...`. Confidence medium: the deferred-read crash is confirmed by static read of the delegate + lambda capture; whether a live state transition can actually null the listing while the button is on screen was not runtime-verified.

routes/budgets.rs returns the raw internal error string to the HTTP client on EVERY database-error branch: `Json(ErrorResponse::new("DB_ERROR", e.to_string()))` appears 37 times (first at budgets.rs:260 in create_budget, then repeated across list_budgets/get_budget/update_budget/delete_budget/submit/approve/activate/close/summary/category_variance/variance_alerts/add_item/list_items/update_item/delete_item/record_actual/list_actuals/create_category/list_categories and the rest of the handlers), each paired with `StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (grep counts 37 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR sites in the file). The error is ALSO already logged server-side (`tracing::error!("Failed to create budget: {:?}", e)` etc.), so the client-body copy is pure over-exposure.

The `e` here is the repository error (sqlx-backed budget_repo calls such as create_budget_rls / list_budgets_rls). `sqlx::Error::Database(...).to_string()` renders the Postgres message, which routinely includes table names, column names, constraint names and SQL fragments — returning it verbatim in the response body is a schema/information-disclosure leak to any authenticated caller who can trip a DB error (e.g. a constraint violation), and it diverges from the codebase's own safe pattern (e.g. ai/voice.rs:204-213 deliberately logs the detail but returns a static OAUTH_EXCHANGE_FAILED_MESSAGE to the client).

Same defect CLASS as the accepted 2026-08-31 finding code-review-api-handlers-compliance-raw-db-error-leak, but a DISTINCT and much larger file: compliance.rs was one file; budgets.rs is the single worst offender with 37 leak sites and was not touched by that run. Fix: replace the `e.to_string()` body with a static message (e.g. `ErrorResponse::new("DB_ERROR", "Failed to process budget request")`) and keep the existing `tracing::error!` for the detail. IG3: an integration test that forces a budget repo error (e.g. duplicate/constraint violation on create_budget) asserts the 500 response body does NOT contain SQL/schema tokens (table/column/constraint names).

Confidence medium: the 37 `e.to_string()` client-body sites and their 500 status are confirmed by static read; reachability to the client is certain (they are in the handler's Err arm returned directly via into_response()). Severity medium (+2) rather than high because it is information disclosure to an authenticated caller (no auth bypass, no data loss, no crash), and the exact sensitivity of the leaked strings depends on which sqlx error is surfaced.

routes/oauth.rs leaks the raw internal error string to the client on the OAuth-provider client-management endpoints — the most security-sensitive surface in this segment: register_client (POST /clients) returns `Json(ErrorResponse::new("REGISTRATION_FAILED", e.to_string()))` at oauth.rs:724, update_client (PUT /clients/{id}) at :874 (`UPDATE_FAILED`), revoke_client (DELETE /clients/{id}) at :954 (`REVOKE_FAILED`, HTTP 500), and regenerate_client_secret at :1024 (`REGENERATE_FAILED`, HTTP 500). Each already logs the detail server-side (`tracing::error!(error = %e, "Failed to register OAuth client")` etc.), so the client-body copy is redundant exposure.

These handlers wrap `state.oauth_service` calls (register_client/update_client/revoke_client/regenerate_client_secret), whose errors are sqlx/service errors; `e.to_string()` on them can expose oauth-client table/column/constraint internals to the API caller. Because this is the OAuth authorization-server admin surface (routes confirmed live: `.route("/clients", post(register_client))` at oauth.rs:55, `.route("/clients/{id}", ...)`), leaking backend error internals here is higher-value to an attacker probing the auth subsystem than on an ordinary CRUD route.

Distinct from the budgets.rs finding (different file, different endpoints, auth-provider surface) and from the accepted 2026-08-31 compliance.rs finding. Part of the broader 24-file `ErrorResponse::new(..., e.to_string())` surface noted in this run's `note`, but called out separately because the OAuth admin endpoints warrant their own fix/priority. Fix: return static messages (REGISTRATION_FAILED / UPDATE_FAILED / REVOKE_FAILED / REGENERATE_FAILED) with the detail kept only in the existing tracing logs. IG3: a test that forces an oauth_service error on register_client asserts the response body carries no SQL/schema tokens.

Confidence medium: the four `e.to_string()` client-body sites and their status codes are confirmed by static read, and the routes are confirmed reachable via the router builder in the same file. Severity medium (+2): information disclosure on the auth-provider surface (no auth bypass or token leak proven statically — the leaked strings are backend error messages, not credentials — so not high).

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/person-months/PersonMonthsScreen.tsx — 197-line user-facing screen imports NO useTranslation and makes ZERO t() calls (grep useTranslation=0, t(=0), so every string renders English for sk/cs/de/en users. This is a whole-screen gap, not a leak: the mobile app ships react-i18next with locales/ for all four languages and the rest of screens/ is localized.
Hardcoded UI text: L93 <Text>Person-months</Text> (screen header), L142 'Save', L145 'Cancel', L155 'Edit', L165 'Bulk entry…' (primary action buttons).
Hardcoded validation Alert: L78 Alert.alert('Invalid value', 'Enter a whole number between 0 and 20.') — the only feedback a user gets on bad input is English-only.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/settings/WidgetSettingsScreen.tsx — imports useTranslation and makes only 2 t() calls, yet hardcodes most of its user-facing text: the component is partially localized, so the leaks render English on a 4-locale app while the surrounding chrome is translated (a worse look than a fully-untranslated screen).
Hardcoded section/heading text: L89/L105/L126 <Text>Widget Settings</Text>, L109 'Widgets Not Available', L131 'Available Widgets', L163 'Active Widgets', L194 'How to Add Widgets'.
Hardcoded Alerts: L66 Alert.alert('Widget Added', `${name} widget has been configured.`) and L79 Alert.alert('Widgets Updated', 'All widgets have been refreshed.').

Fix: route every literal (headings + both Alert.alert title/body pairs) through the already-imported t() with settings.widgets.* keys and backfill locales/{sk,cs,de,en}. Confidence medium: leaks confirmed by static read; Low severity (i18n).

ppt-web has NO global auth gate: App.tsx:272-275 renders `<RouteErrorBoundary><Suspense><AppRoutes/></Suspense></RouteErrorBoundary>` inside the always-rendered app shell (the shell only toggles header UI on `isAuthenticated`, App.tsx:164/173/183). AppRoutes.tsx:39-67 composes every feature route-group fragment flat under a single `<Routes>` with no enclosing `<Route element={<ProtectedRoute/>}>` parent. So the ONLY auth gate for a feature route is a per-route `<ProtectedRoute>` wrapper inside its group file.

ProtectedRoute.tsx:92-122 is the gate: when `!isLoading && !isAuthenticated` it stores the return URL and `return <Navigate to={redirectTo} replace/>` (redirect to /login). Groups that wrap each element in it therefore bounce unauthenticated users to login — e.g. buildings.tsx:47-80 wraps every `<Route element={<ProtectedRoute>…</ProtectedRoute>}/>`; same in leases.tsx, meters.tsx, documents.tsx, rentals.tsx (auth guard added by PR #2648), reports.tsx, voting.tsx, person-months.tsx, core.tsx, notifications.tsx.

11 route groups mount their pages as BARE `<Route element={<…PageRoute/>}/>` with ZERO ProtectedRoute wrapper (grep `ProtectedRoute` count = 0 in each): financial.tsx:466-474 (/financial, /financial/invoices, /financial/payments, /financial/budgets, /financial/reports), accounting.tsx:9-14 (/accounting/invoices, /accounting/payment-matching), faults.tsx, community.tsx, disputes.tsx, iot.tsx, messaging.tsx, neighbors.tsx, outages.tsx, announcements.tsx, ai-dashboards.tsx. An unauthenticated user navigating directly to e.g. /financial or /accounting/invoices is NOT redirected to login — the authenticated-only page shell renders instead.

The financial wrappers do not self-guard: FinancialDashboardPageRoute (financial.tsx:66-68) only does `const { user } = useAuth(); const orgId = user?.organizationId ?? ''` and gates its money queries with `enabled: !!orgId` (financial.tsx:73/78/83); InvoiceManagement/PaymentManagement/FinancialReports wrappers (financial.tsx:148/257/384) follow the same read-only `user?.…` pattern with no `if (!isAuthenticated) return <Navigate/>`. There is no internal redirect anywhere in the group.

Data-leak is BOUNDED, which is why this is scored medium (+2) not high: with no `user` the org-scoped queries stay disabled (`enabled:!!orgId` with orgId='') and the reality-server/api-server require auth (401), so no tenant financial data is actually fetched or shown to an anonymous visitor. The defect is a broken-access-control / missing-redirect posture bug (CWE-284): protected app surfaces are reachable without authentication and render a broken empty shell instead of sending the user to /login (and losing the return-URL capture that ProtectedRoute.tsx:43-49 provides). Money-sensitive surfaces (financial, accounting) are among the unguarded set.

This is a distinct, systemic, LANDABLE finding — not the same as the done route items (security-role-gate-fail-open = ProtectedRoute's own role check; code-review-ppt-web-ui-protectedroute-i18n = untranslated gate copy; screen-map-drift-pr-2648-ppt = rentals-only mutation guard). Mechanical fix: wrap each `<Route>` element in these 11 group files with `<ProtectedRoute>` (importing from '../../components'), mirroring buildings.tsx:47-80, so the whole app enforces auth uniformly at the routing layer. Confidence medium: the missing-wrapper + no-global-gate mechanism is code-verified end to end (App.tsx -> AppRoutes -> group -> ProtectedRoute), but the exact anonymous-visitor render is not runtime-confirmed (static analysis, no execution).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/facilities/pages/FacilitiesPage.tsx:36-41 — `useIsManager()` is a hardcoded stub: `// Placeholder: Returns true during development to enable all manager features. // Replace with actual role check when AuthContext is implemented for ppt-web.` and the body is simply `return true;`. It is not gated behind a dev-only flag or feature flag — it ships as-is.

This page is wired and reachable in production: mounted via routes/groups/buildings.tsx and routes/lazyRoutes.tsx (Epic 56 Facility Booking). `isManager` (line 46) is passed straight into `<FacilityList isManager={isManager} ... onCreate={handleCreate} onEdit={handleEdit} />` (lines 110-124), which — per the sibling component contract used across the app — controls whether manager-only actions (Create Facility, Edit) render for the current viewer.

Effect: every visitor to /buildings/:buildingId/facilities — resident or manager — sees and can click Create/Edit facility controls. The comment claims 'Backend still enforces authorization - this is for UI display only', so a resident's click likely 403s rather than succeeding, but the UI still exposes manager-only affordances and navigates to /facilities/new or /facilities/:id/edit for a plain resident, producing a confusing broken-looking flow (form opens, submit silently fails) instead of the buttons simply not being there. Not verified at runtime whether every backend facility-mutation endpoint actually enforces the role check (static read only) — confidence medium.

Fix: wire the real role check (the file's own docstring gives the exact replacement — `const { user } = useAuth(); return user?.role === 'manager' || user?.role === 'admin';`, mirroring frontend/apps/mobile/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx) instead of the permanent `return true` stub.

RegistryPage.tsx:17-21 and RegistryRulesPage.tsx:16-20 both instantiate `const registryApi = createRegistryApi({ baseUrl: API_BASE_URL, // accessToken and tenantId would come from auth context });` at MODULE scope (evaluated once at import time), with no accessToken or tenantId ever supplied — the comment is a live TODO, not a resolved wiring.

packages/api-client/src/registry/api.ts:29-33,43-45 — `buildHeaders(config)` builds `Authorization`/`X-Tenant-ID` headers ONLY if `config.accessToken`/`config.tenantId` are truthy, and `createRegistryApi` calls `buildHeaders(config)` exactly once and closes over the resulting static `headers` object for every subsequent pets/vehicles/rules request (list/get/create/update/delete/review). Unlike the rest of the app's api-client modules (e.g. faults/hooks.ts -> faults/api.ts), which resolve auth per-request through a shared client, this factory bakes auth in at construction and never refreshes it.

Net effect: every request the Building Registries feature (Epic 57 — pet/vehicle registration list, create, update, delete, review, and registry-rules read/update) makes goes out with NO Authorization header and NO tenant header, guaranteed to 401 (or hit the wrong/default tenant scope if the backend doesn't strictly require the header) the moment this feature is routed into the app.

Currently reduces to a latent landmine rather than a live incident: grepping frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/ and docs/screens/ppt/ turns up no route or screen-map entry for RegistryPage/RegistryRulesPage — the feature is not mounted in the router today, so this specific defect has no current production reachability. Flagging now because it is a real, non-obvious footgun for whoever wires the route next (the module-scope singleton pattern silently swallows the missing token instead of erroring). Fix: build the api instance from a hook/context that supplies a live accessToken/tenantId (matching the pattern other wired features use) rather than a frozen module-level singleton.

Confidence medium: the missing-auth-header logic is confirmed by static read of buildHeaders/createRegistryApi; actual backend response behavior (hard 401 vs silent wrong-tenant read) is not verified without execution.

EditFacilityPage.tsx has NO `useTranslation` import at all (checked full file) — every user-facing string is hardcoded English: 'Edit Facility' (line 89 heading), 'Failed to load facility' (line 30, set as the error banner text), 'Failed to update facility' (line 50, mutation-error fallback), 'Facility not found' (line 74), 'Go back' (line 80). This is the sole page under features/facilities/pages that skips i18n entirely — its siblings (BookFacilityPage, FacilitiesPage's FacilityList) at least partially use `t()`.

BookFacilityPage.tsx does import `useTranslation` and wraps the page title (line 128, `t('facilities.bookings.bookFacility')`), but every error/fallback string is still hardcoded English: 'Failed to load facility details' (line 35), 'Failed to create booking' (line 71, mutation fallback), 'Facility not found' (line 95), 'This facility is not available for booking' (line 112), 'Go back' (lines 101, 118) — i.e. i18n is wired but not applied to the error-path copy on this file specifically.

Both pages are wired and reachable in production (routes/groups/buildings.tsx + routes/lazyRoutes.tsx, Epic 56 Facility Booking) — an sk/cs/de-locale user who hits any facility-load or booking/update error sees raw English copy on a mounted, everyday manager/resident flow.

Same defect class as prior ppt-web-ui i18n-gap findings (e.g. 2026-09-01 notif-settings-hardcoded-errors) but a distinct, previously-unreviewed feature area. Fix: add `useTranslation` to EditFacilityPage.tsx and move all listed strings (both files) into an i18n namespace. Confidence medium: hardcoded-string presence confirmed by static read; exact end-user visibility depends on which error path fires at runtime.

get_suggestions (routes/listings.rs:457-480, GET /api/v1/listings/suggestions, public/anonymous search-suggestions endpoint consumed by reality-web) returns a `popular_searches` list that is a hardcoded Slovak-only literal vec (:474-478): `"2-izbový byt Bratislava"`, `"Dom Košice"`, `"Pozemok Žilina"`. These are user-facing suggestion strings rendered verbatim by the client, and they are returned identically regardless of the caller's locale. reality-web ships SIX locale bundles (frontend/apps/reality-web/messages/: sk, cs, de, en, hu, pl), so a de/en/cs/hu/pl portal visitor is shown Slovak search suggestions with no way to localize them — the strings are baked server-side, not returned as translatable keys.

The same handler hardcodes the nearby-city fallback to a Slovak city: `let city = params.get("city")...unwrap_or("Bratislava")` (:461-464), then feeds it to `get_nearby_cities(city, 10)` (:466-468). reality-server is explicitly multi-region (backend/CLAUDE.md + REGION env supports sk/cz/eu; reality-portal.cz and reality-portal.eu are first-class default CORS origins), so on a Czech (.cz) or EU (.eu) deployment a suggestion request that omits `city` seeds nearby-city suggestions from Bratislava (SK) rather than a region-appropriate default — wrong-country content, not merely untranslated. This is a region-awareness correctness defect on top of the i18n gap.

Distinct from every prior reality-server finding: the recent i18n finding (alert-drainer-i18n-english-only, 2026-08-30) is in services/search_alert_drainer.rs + email.rs, and the prior listings.rs findings (viewcount-hardcoded-zero, orphan-listinghandler-stub-detail, pagination-offset-overflow — all done) touch different handlers. No prior signal or backlog row references get_suggestions / popular_searches. Fix: return `popular_searches` as translatable keys (or derive them from actual popular queries per region) instead of Slovak literals, and make the default city region-derived (from REGION / host) rather than the constant "Bratislava". IG3: a request to /api/v1/listings/suggestions on a non-SK region (or with an Accept-Language other than sk) asserts the suggestions/default-city are not the Slovak Bratislava literals.

Confidence medium: the hardcoded Slovak literals and the Bratislava default are confirmed by static read of the full handler; severity medium (+2) rather than low because the Bratislava default produces wrong-region content on the cz/eu deployments (a correctness issue), not only an untranslated string — but not high because the endpoint is a non-critical public suggestions helper (no auth, no data loss, no crash).

get_categories (routes/listings.rs:776-820, GET /api/v1/listings/categories, public/anonymous endpoint) populates each CategoryCount.label via label_for_property_type (:822-837), which is a hardcoded Slovak-only match: apartment->"Byty", house->"Domy", land->"Pozemky", commercial->"Komerčné priestory", office->"Kancelárie", garage->"Garáže", parking->"Parkovanie", storage->"Sklady". The CategoryCount.label field doc-comment (:569-570) even states 'Localized display label (Slovak — primary market)', confirming this is a known single-locale shortcut. The handler takes only State (:776-778) — no Accept-Language header, no locale query param — so the Slovak labels are returned identically to every caller.

reality-web renders these labels directly (CategoryCount matches the client's CategoryCount type per :561) and ships six locale bundles (sk, cs, de, en, hu, pl). Because the label is pre-localized to Slovak server-side rather than returned as a translatable key, a cs/de/en/hu/pl portal user sees Slovak category names ('Byty', 'Domy', ...) with no client-side path to translate them. The `icon` field already returns the raw property_type key (:811) — i.e. the untranslated enum key IS available to the client — so the correct shape is to let the client translate the property_type key and drop (or make optional/locale-negotiated) the server-baked Slovak label.

Distinct from the sibling get_suggestions finding (different handler, different endpoint, different fix) and from all prior reality-server findings (no signal or backlog row references label_for_property_type / get_categories). Fix: either return only the property_type key and let reality-web's next-intl bundles localize it, or negotiate the label off an Accept-Language header instead of hardcoding Slovak. IG3: /api/v1/listings/categories with Accept-Language: en (or de) asserts labels are not the Slovak literals (or that the response exposes the raw property_type key for client-side translation).

Confidence medium: the Slovak-only match arm and the locale-unaware handler signature are confirmed by static read; severity low (+1) — a pure i18n label gap on a public helper endpoint (no auth, no correctness/region impact beyond display language), lower than the get_suggestions finding which additionally serves wrong-region city data.

RealtorManagement.tsx RealtorDetailModal has three destructive/state-changing handlers that await mutateAsync with NO try/catch: handleSave (updateRealtor.mutateAsync, L829-834 then setIsEditing(false)), handleRemove (removeRealtor.mutateAsync, L838-839 then onClose()), handleStatusChange (updateRealtor.mutateAsync, L843-847).

updateRealtor.error / removeRealtor.error are NEVER read or rendered anywhere in the file (grep for '.error'/'.isError' finds only the mutateAsync call sites). On a failed remove-realtor or status-change the row/modal silently fails to update, the follow-up setState (setIsEditing(false)/onClose) never runs, and mutateAsync (unlike mutate) rejects -> unhandled promise rejection in a React event handler (React does not surface those).
The backing hooks useUpdateRealtor (agency/hooks.ts:307) and useRemoveRealtor (:333) define onSuccess (invalidateQueries) only, NO onError, so error surfacing is entirely the caller's responsibility.

The invite modal in the SAME file (handleSubmit, L568-580) already shows the correct pattern: try/catch around inviteRealtor.mutateAsync with setInviteError(t('inviteError')) rendered inline. Fix: mirror that pattern in the DetailModal handlers (try/catch, only run the follow-up setState on success, render an inline error using the existing t('inviteError')/agency namespace). removeRealtor is an irreversible action, so silent failure is the worst case.

AgencyBranding.tsx handleSave (L79-95) does `await updateBranding.mutateAsync({ agencyId, data: { logo, coverImage, primaryColor, ... } })` with NO try/catch, then resets hasChanges/logoFile/coverFile.

get_mfa_status_report (routes/compliance.rs:671-711, GDPR/security MFA-adoption report) computes its two aggregates over DIFFERENT populations: mfa_enabled = SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_2fa WHERE enabled = true (:678-685) counts every 2FA row regardless of the owning user's status, while total_users = SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE status = 'active' (:688-695) counts only active users. It then derives mfa_disabled = total_users - mfa_enabled (:697) and adoption_rate = mfa_enabled / total_users * 100 (:698-702).

Because the numerator (all enabled-2FA rows, including suspended / pending / soft-deleted / deactivated users that still have a user_2fa row) is drawn from a superset of the denominator (active users only), the report can produce nonsensical figures: mfa_disabled_count can go NEGATIVE and adoption_rate can exceed 100%. Even short of those extremes the adoption rate is systematically inflated whenever any inactive user retains an enabled 2FA row.

Odd-one-out within the same file: the sibling get_privacy_settings_report (:509-560) correctly scopes BOTH numerator and denominator to WHERE status = 'active'. Fix: scope the mfa_enabled count to active users too via JOIN users u ON u.id = t.user_id WHERE t.enabled = true AND u.status = 'active'. IG3: seed one active user with 2FA, one SUSPENDED user with 2FA, one active user without 2FA -> expect mfa_enabled_count==1, total_users==2, mfa_disabled_count==1, adoption_rate==50.0 (currently 2/0/100.0).
Confidence medium; severity medium (+2): corrupts a compliance/security metric (possible negative/over-100% values) rather than crashing or leaking data. Platform-admin-gated.

get_audit_summary (routes/compliance.rs:229-265) obtains integrity_verified via state.audit_log_repo.verify_integrity(Some(1000)).await.unwrap_or(false) (:252-256). Unlike every other fallible call in this file (which propagate through .map_err(db_error)?), this SWALLOWS any error and coerces it to false.

Consequence: a false-negative on a security/compliance signal. A transient DB error, lock timeout, or any failure inside verify_integrity is reported as integrity_verified: false -- as if the audit-log hash chain had been TAMPERED with -- when the check merely failed to run. That can trigger incident response for a non-event and masks the real DB error. The dedicated verify_audit_integrity handler (:339-364) correctly propagates with .map_err(db_error)?, so the summary handler is the inconsistent one.

Fix: propagate the error (.map_err(db_error)?) so a check failure returns 500 rather than masquerading as an integrity violation; or model integrity as tri-state (verified / violated / check-unavailable). IG3: force verify_integrity to error and assert the endpoint does NOT return integrity_verified:false-with-200.
Confidence medium; severity medium (+2): misreports a security-integrity signal (false tamper alarm) and hides the real error; platform-admin-gated, not a crash or data leak.

get_audit_logs (routes/compliance.rs:158-209) parses the client action filter via let action = params.action.and_then(|a| parse_audit_action(&a)); (:164). parse_audit_action (:809-843) returns None for any string not in its match table. backend/crates/db/src/repositories/vote.rs:224-278 cast_vote_rls INSERTs into vote_responses using the caller-supplied unit_id and user_id verbatim, sets `vote_weight = COALESCE((SELECT ownership_share FROM units WHERE id = $3), 1.0)` (so the ballot even takes the TARGET unit's ownership weight), and uses `ON CONFLICT (vote_id, unit_id) DO UPDATE SET user_id = EXCLUDED.user_id, answers = EXCLUDED.answers, ...`. The only isolation is org-level RLS on the vote_responses insert (via rls.conn()); RLS is tenant-scoped, NOT unit-owner-scoped. Consequence: any authenticated member of the tenant can cast a ballot for a unit they do not own, and — via the ON CONFLICT overwrite — silently replace another owner's already-cast ballot for that unit, changing the weighted outcome of a legally-significant owner vote (Slovak building governance). This is ballot stuffing / vote fraud, an authorization bypass on a data-integrity-critical path.

This is an INCONSISTENCY, not an intended design: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/delegations.rs:207-233 create_delegation already enforces exactly the missing check — `state.<unit_repo>.get_owners_rls(&mut **rls.conn(), unit_id)` then `let is_owner = owners.iter().any(|o| o.user_id == auth.user_id)` returning 403 'You must be an owner of the unit ...'. Fix: after loading `existing`, when delegation_id is None, look up owners of req.unit_id on the RLS connection and reject with 403 unless rls.user_id() is an owner (mirror delegations.rs). IG3: an integration test where user A (owner of unit U1) POSTs /voting/{id}/cast with unit_id = U2 (owned by user B) must receive 403 and leave U2's ballot untouched; it fails on main today (the insert succeeds).

Confidence high: the full call path was traced statically from the mounted route (voting.rs:47) through the handler (voting.rs:1067) into the repository INSERT (vote.rs:224). Severity high (+3): authorization bypass enabling silent tampering with weighted vote results (integrity/data-corruption on a governance surface), reachable by any authenticated tenant member.

Every suspend function in shared/commonMain repositories that wraps a Ktor call uses the pattern `try { ... } catch (e: Exception) { Result.failure(e) }` WITHOUT first rethrowing CancellationException. Grep confirms 57 `catch (e: Exception)` sites across 9 repository files; grep for `CancellationException` across the same tree returns hits ONLY in LayoutRepository.kt (the sole file that does it right).

Per-file catch counts: ApiClient 6, SsoService 9, ListingRepository 6, InquiryRepository 8, FavoritesRepository 11, NotificationRepository 9, AgencyRepository 4, PortalListingsRepository 2, RealtorRepository 2. Reference correct pattern: mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/layout/LayoutRepository.kt:65-69 — `} catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e } catch (e: Exception) { ... }` with a covering test at commonTest/.../LayoutRepositoryTest.kt:266 asserting cancellation propagates.

Impact — coroutine cancellation is silently converted to `Result.failure(CancellationException)`. In Compose, LaunchedEffect / rememberCoroutineScope callers that navigate away or key-change during a network fetch will (a) let the network work run to completion instead of being cancelled, (b) still fold the 'failure' branch into `errorMessage = friendlyError(it)`, potentially surfacing a spurious error toast/banner for a screen the user already left, and (c) violate structured concurrency in a way that will surface as flakiness under load / weak-network conditions. This is a canonical KMP anti-pattern (see kotlinx.coroutines Result docs + Ktor error-handling guidance).

Fix: add the two-catch pattern (`catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }` before `catch (e: Exception)`) to every listed site; add a shared extension helper `suspend fun <T> runNetworkCatching(block: suspend () -> T): Result<T>` in util/ that encapsulates it, then migrate call sites. Confidence medium — the anti-pattern is confirmed statically for every listed site; the runtime effect (spurious error banners) is highly likely but not runtime-confirmed.

lib/api.ts:321 `export default getApiClient();` is evaluated at module-import time. getApiClient() (api.ts:273-278) lazily builds the singleton via createAxiosInstance() with NO config, which as a side effect sets the module-level `tokenGetter = undefined` and `onUnauthorizedCallback = undefined` (api.ts:195-196) and pins baseURL to DEFAULT_BASE_URL / timeout to DEFAULT_TIMEOUT. So merely importing this module eagerly instantiates an unconfigured axios instance and mutates module globals before AuthContext ever calls configureApiClient().

configureApiClient() (api.ts:298-301) reassigns `apiInstance` to a BRAND-NEW instance. The default export binding, however, is frozen to the FIRST (import-time) instance. The two instances only behave identically today because both interceptors read the same module-level `tokenGetter`/`onUnauthorizedCallback` (api.ts:201/219) and AuthContext.configureApiClient (AuthContext.tsx:352-355) passes no baseURL/timeout override. Any future call passing a custom baseURL, timeout, or per-instance interceptor to configureApiClient() would silently NOT apply to default-export consumers, and resetApiClient() (api.ts:307-311, called on AuthProvider unmount, AuthContext.tsx:360) nulls `apiInstance` + clears the globals, orphaning the default export so its interceptors read cleared globals (requests without Authorization).

Landability confirmed: a repo-wide grep for a default import of lib/api (`import api ...` / `import api, {` from lib/api) returns ZERO consumers — every call site uses the named getApiClient() export. The default export is dead code whose only effect is the import-time instantiation + global mutation. Safe pure-frontend fix: drop `export default getApiClient();` (or export the function `getApiClient` itself, not its invocation) so the singleton is created only when configureApiClient()/getApiClient() is first called. Low severity (+1): no runtime bug is currently reachable, but it is a footgun that defeats the single-source-of-truth intent documented in AuthContext.tsx:337-355. Confidence medium: mechanism verified statically end-to-end (module eval order + interceptor closures over module globals), not runtime-executed.

Asymmetric wire contract: on RECEIVE, parseServerMessage (websocket.ts:65-82) treats the canonical server frame as `{ event, payload }` and maps `event` -> internal `type`. On SEND, WebSocketService.send (websocket.ts:444-457) does `this.socket.send(JSON.stringify(message))` where `message` is the internal WebSocketMessage shape `{ type, payload, timestamp }` (websocket.ts:38-43) — it is emitted verbatim with a `type` key, never re-mapped back to the server's `{ event, payload }` envelope. A server that parses inbound frames as WsEvent `{ event, payload }` (mirroring ws_notifications.rs) would see `event: undefined` and drop/ignore the frame.

The send path is fully wired through the public API — WebSocketContext.send (WebSocketContext.tsx:371-378) delegates to service.send, and useWebSocket / its sibling hooks re-export `send` to consumers (hooks/useWebSocket.ts:76/101/130/165/189) — so this is a live, callable surface, not private code.

Currently LATENT, hence low (+1): a repo-wide grep for `.send(` shows the only call site is WebSocketContext.tsx:377 (the delegation itself); no feature code sends a domain message today because the notifications socket is effectively server->client. But the first consumer to call `send({...})` will hit a silent no-op (frame accepted by the client, ignored by the server) with no error surfaced. Landable pure-frontend fix: have send() serialize the server envelope shape (`{ event: message.type, payload: message.payload }`) to match parseServerMessage's inbound contract, mirroring the documented WsEvent envelope, or narrow the exported API to remove the unsupported send until a client->server protocol exists. Confidence medium: the shape mismatch is code-verified against parseServerMessage + the WebSocketMessage/ServerWsEnvelope interfaces; the server-side reject is inferred from the documented envelope, not runtime-confirmed.

evidence: list_import_jobs (routes/imports.rs:115-135, GET /api/v1/imports/jobs) is a PAGINATED endpoint — it reads query.limit.unwrap_or(20) and clamp_offset_i32(query.offset) (:124-126) and fetches a single page via reality_portal_repo.list_import_jobs(user_id, status, limit, offset). It then computes the pagination total as `let total = jobs.len() as i64;` (:131) and returns ImportJobsResponse { jobs, total } (:133). total therefore equals the size of the CURRENT PAGE (at most `limit`, default 20), NOT the true number of import jobs for the user.

Consequence: any client that computes page count as ceil(total / limit) sees total==20 on every full page (and total==remainder on the last), concludes there is exactly one page, and never requests offset=20,40,... — silently hiding every import job beyond the first page from the agency/realtor UI. On a user with, say, 55 import jobs the list appears to contain only 20. This is the same class of defect already confirmed in the sibling api-server compliance handler (code-review-api-handlers-user-audit-logs-total-page-len), here on the reality-server imports surface.

Fix: back total with a real count query (e.g. a reality_portal_repo.count_import_jobs(user_id, status) mirroring the filter), not the page length. IG3: an integration test seeding N>limit import jobs for one user asserts response.total == N while response.jobs.len() == limit. Distinct from the known 2026-08-31 reality-server pagination finding (which was about OFFSET integer overflow / clamping, since fixed via util::clamp_offset_i32 used right here at :126) — this is the response `total` field being wrong, an orthogonal bug.

Confidence medium: the paginated fetch (limit+offset) and the page-length-as-total computation are confirmed by static read of the full handler; medium (not high) because the surface is auth-gated (PortalPrincipal) and the harm is a corrupted pagination contract / under-exposed list rather than a crash, data loss, or cross-tenant leak.

The agency import-history handler (routes/agency_imports.rs, around :165-190) runs a hand-written query `SELECT ... FROM portal_import_jobs WHERE agency_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 100` (:170-176) and then reports `let total = rows.len() as i64;` (:183) as the response total. There is no offset/limit query param and no count query: the endpoint hard-caps the returned history at 100 rows and sets total = min(actual_rows, 100).

Consequence: once an agency accumulates more than 100 import jobs, the import-history view silently drops everything older than the 100 most-recent, and `total` misreports the real number of jobs as 100 — there is no pagination affordance and no signal to the client that the list was truncated. For a busy agency running recurring feed imports this hides the bulk of the audit trail. Lower severity than the imports.rs:131 finding because the truncation is a fixed cap (no client-side page-count miscomputation), but it is a distinct handler and a distinct silent-data-loss-on-read defect.

Fix: either add real pagination (limit+offset params + a COUNT(*) for total, mirroring list_import_jobs once that is corrected) or, at minimum, surface a `truncated`/`has_more` flag and derive total from a COUNT(*) rather than rows.len(). IG3: an integration test seeding >100 portal_import_jobs for one agency asserts the response exposes the true count (or a has_more flag) instead of a flat total==100.

Confidence medium: the LIMIT 100 literal and total=rows.len() are confirmed by static read; medium severity capped at +1 because the surface is membership-gated (check_agency_membership at :168) and the impact is truncated read visibility rather than a crash or cross-tenant leak.

evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/notification_digest.rs:130-154 — NotificationDigestWorker::start() spawns the sweep on every process, and its own module doc (lines 6-9) states it 'mirrors the PushFanoutWorker / QuietHoursDrainWorker lifecycle', i.e. it runs on every api-server replica. Unlike the sibling QuietHoursDrainWorker — which delivers each held row exactly once across replicas by *atomically claiming* rows via GranularNotificationRepository::claim_notifications_to_release (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, issue #2831, drain code at quiet_hours_drain.rs:150-172) — the digest worker fetches rows with plain, unlocked SELECTs and never claims them, so concurrent replicas process the same rows.

Retry path double-sends: notification_digest.rs:176-217 retry_unsent() calls GranularNotificationRepository::get_unsent_digests (granular_notification.rs:973-1002), which is a plain `SELECT ... WHERE d.email_sent_at IS NULL AND d.created_at > $1 ... LIMIT $2` with no FOR UPDATE / SKIP LOCKED / claim stamp. Two replicas ticking within the same window both fetch the identical set of unsent digest rows and both call email_service.send_digest_email before either calls mark_digest_email_sent (the mark happens only after a successful async send, lines 205-210) — so the same user receives the digest email N times, once per replica.

New-digest path is a check-then-act (TOCTOU) race: notification_digest.rs:222-300 send_new() relies on the `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM notification_digests d WHERE d.user_id = u.id AND d.created_at > $2)` guard inside find_inactive_digest_candidates (granular_notification.rs:908-965) to avoid re-digesting a user within the resend window. That SELECT and the subsequent create_digest INSERT (line 259-272) are not atomic and take no row lock, and create_digest (granular_notification.rs:824+) shows no ON CONFLICT / unique-constraint guard — so two replicas that both evaluate the candidate query before either INSERTs both see NOT EXISTS = true, both persist a digest row, and both email it.

Impact: under the project's documented multi-replica api-server deployment (the exact scenario #2831 hardened the held-notification drain against) inactive users receive duplicate 24h-inactivity digest emails. Severity medium (annoyance / spam-perception, not data loss; single-replica deploys are unaffected). Confidence medium: the absence of any claim/lock/ON-CONFLICT is confirmed by static read of both the worker and the two repository queries; the duplicate delivery is inferred from concurrent execution, not runtime-confirmed. Fix: give the digest worker the same exactly-once discipline as QuietHoursDrainWorker — claim rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (or an atomic UPDATE ... RETURNING that stamps a claim/sent marker) in get_unsent_digests, and make create_digest idempotent via a unique constraint on (user_id, digest_type, period) + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so the send_new race collapses to a single row.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/notification_digest.rs:176-217 — retry_unsent() re-attempts only the digest rows returned by get_unsent_digests(resend_cutoff, ...), and get_unsent_digests (granular_notification.rs:973-1002) filters `d.created_at > $1` where $1 = now - resend_window_hours (default 20h, config at notification_digest.rs:52/63/89-92). A digest row whose email send keeps failing (permanently-invalid recipient address, SMTP hard-reject, provider outage longer than the window) is retried each tick only until its created_at ages past resend_cutoff; after that it is never selected again, so email_sent_at stays NULL forever.

There is no terminal handling for such a row: no attempt counter, no dead-letter, no error metric, and no alert — the row is simply left email_sent_at = NULL and silently forgotten. The only trace is a per-attempt tracing::warn! at line 212-214 ('will retry next tick'), which stops firing once the row ages out. The user's unread notifications therefore never produce a delivered digest for that window, with no operator signal that a digest was dropped.

This is the exact failure mode the sibling held-notification drain path was hardened against: quiet_hours_drain.rs:226-279 (record_failure/dead_letter) bumps an attempt counter and dead-letters a permanently-failing row after max_attempts (issue #2823) instead of dropping it. The digest worker adopted that cluster's lifecycle and retry-in-place idea but not its give-up/dead-letter accounting. Severity low (a digest is a redundant convenience — the underlying notifications remain available in-app — and a fresh digest may be generated in a later window once the row ages out), confidence medium (the silent-abandon boundary is confirmed by static read of the worker + the created_at>cutoff query filter; the permanent-failure trigger is inferred, not runtime-confirmed). Fix: track attempts on notification_digests and dead-letter / emit a metric when a digest exhausts its retry budget, mirroring the #2823 held-notification treatment.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/tenant_config.rs:222-238 - fetch_organization_name() acquires a pooled connection (pool.acquire) and enables SYSTEM RLS context on it via db::tenant_context::set_request_context(&mut *conn, None, None, true) at line 224 (the 4th arg `true` = system/RLS-bypass context, used here to read the organizations table across tenants for an org-name lookup).

tenant_context.rs:237 - after the query, the reset is fire-and-forget: `let _ = db::tenant_context::clear_request_context(&mut *conn).await;`. The Result is discarded, so a failed clear is neither retried nor logged, and the PoolConnection is then dropped and returned to the pool still carrying the system-context session flag.

This is the ONLY system-context call site in the crate that swallows the clear. Every sibling logs the failure via `if let Err(e) = clear_request_context(...) { tracing::warn!/error!(...) }`: admin_tenants.rs:243/311/361, agency_provisioning.rs:282, signatures.rs:1145, admin/users.rs:255, caddy_ask.rs:286 (host_in_verifying_state), and the scheduler fallback at services/scheduler/mod.rs:1396. The scheduler comment at services/scheduler/mod.rs:2024 states the clear 'resets the flag before the connection [returns to the pool]', i.e. clearing is the documented contract for not leaking system context into pooled connections.

Impact: if clear_request_context fails (e.g. a mid-statement DB error on the RESET/set_config), the connection re-enters the pool with system RLS-bypass still active. A later request that reuses that connection before its own middleware re-establishes tenant context would run queries with RLS disabled -> potential cross-tenant read. Severity medium: the leak is likely masked in normal operation by per-request context set-up, but the swallow removes the safety net AND hides the failure (no log/metric), which is exactly the observability the sibling sites keep. Confidence medium: the swallow and the divergence from every other site are confirmed by static read; the cross-tenant exposure is conditional on connection reuse without a context reset and is not runtime-confirmed. Fix: mirror the siblings - `if let Err(e) = db::tenant_context::clear_request_context(&mut *conn).await { tracing::warn!(error = %e, "tenant-config: failed to clear system RLS context after org-name lookup"); }` (and consider dropping rather than returning the connection on clear failure).

Saved-search alert matching silently drops matches beyond `config.match_limit` (default 100) in a single cadence window. The worker calls `find_new_match_listing_ids(&query, Some(since), match_limit)` which runs `SELECT l.id ... WHERE l.published_at > $since ORDER BY l.published_at DESC LIMIT $limit` (backend/crates/db/src/repositories/reality_portal/searches.rs:102-121) — returning only the NEWEST `match_limit` matches. It then commits `enqueue_and_advance_saved_search`, whose `mark_saved_search_matched` unconditionally sets `last_matched_at = now()` (searches.rs:185-192). Because the watermark jumps to now() regardless of how many rows the capped query returned, any matching listing ranked 101+ in that window (i.e. published_at between `since` and the 100th-newest match) has published_at <= now() and is excluded from every subsequent run's `published_at > since` filter. Net effect: on a broad saved search over a daily/weekly cadence on an active portal (>100 new matching listings per window is realistic for e.g. 'apartments for rent in Bratislava'), the user is never notified about the older portion of the batch, and `match_count` also undercounts (incremented by the capped listing_ids.len()). Fix options: page the query and advance the watermark only to the oldest UNPROCESSED match's published_at when the cap is hit, or advance last_matched_at to the min(published_at) of the returned rows rather than now() when `rows.len() == match_limit`, so the next run resumes from the truncation boundary instead of skipping past it.

SearchAlertDrainerWorker marks saved-search alerts permanently delivered even when no real notification is sent, creating a silent-loss trap at the transport cutover. The drainer defaults to `LogEmailTransport`/`LogPushTransport` (backend/servers/reality-server/src/services/search_alert_drainer.rs:181-224), whose `send_email`/`send_push` ALWAYS return Ok(()). In `run_once` (lines 358-434) the email stub therefore always sets `any_ok = true`, so every alert row gets `mark_search_alert_notified(alert.id)` (sets notified_at) despite nothing actually leaving the process. This is documented as an intentional first cut, but the forward-looking hazard is NOT addressed: `list_undelivered_search_alerts` filters on notified_at, so when a real SMTP/FCM/APNs adapter is later injected via `with_transports`, every alert queued during the stub period is already notified_at != null and will be skipped forever — those users receive zero first real notification at cutover. Recommend either (a) gate `mark_search_alert_notified` on a transport that reports itself as real (add an `is_real()`/`enabled` seam to the transport traits so the log stubs do NOT advance notified_at), or (b) document a one-time reset of notified_at for the stub-era backlog as part of the real-transport rollout runbook.

Client-side shared-comparison loader trusts an unvalidated network body across the API boundary, inconsistent with the app's own SSR normalizer discipline. ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx:43-47 (frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx) fetches `${getApiBase()}/api/v1/listings/${id}` and returns `response.json() as Promise<ListingSummary>` — a raw runtime cast with NO shape validation — then pushes each result straight into `addToComparison(listing)` (line 70). The SSR sibling that hits the SAME reality-server listing endpoint deliberately does NOT trust the body: getListing() in app/[locale]/listings/[slug]/page.tsx:88-89 runs `parseListingDetail(body)` precisely because 'A 200 does not guarantee a well-formed body: an upstream/proxy partial response or a malformed listing is truthy but may be missing required nested fields ... Rendering such a body crashes SSR with a 500.' The client comparison path has no equivalent guard, so a malformed/partial 200 (or a shape mismatch — note the endpoint returns a listing DETAIL body but this code casts it to the narrower `ListingSummary`) is accepted as valid and can crash the client comparison view when a comparison card dereferences a missing nested field (e.g. address/photos). Fix: validate/normalize the fetched body through the same parser family (a `parseListingSummary`/`parseListingDetail`-style guard) before `addToComparison`, dropping bodies that fail the shape check exactly as `Promise.allSettled` already drops rejected ids, instead of the bare `as Promise<ListingSummary>` cast.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/auth/login/page.tsx:33,72-73 — the login form reads its post-login destination from a user-controlled query param (`const redirectTo = searchParams.get('redirect') ?? '/'`) and, after a successful `login()`, navigates to it with `const safe = redirectTo.startsWith('/') && !redirectTo.startsWith('//') ? redirectTo : '/'; router.replace(safe);`. The guard rejects absolute URLs (`http://…`) and protocol-relative `//evil.com`, but it does NOT reject the backslash-escape form `/\evil.com`. Browsers normalise `\` to `/` during URL resolution, so `router.replace('/\evil.com')` resolves to `//evil.com` → a protocol-relative navigation to an attacker origin. An attacker who gets a victim to open `https://<tenant>/sk/auth/login?redirect=/%5Cevil.example.com` and log in is silently bounced to evil.example.com immediately after authenticating — a classic post-auth open-redirect / phishing primitive.

The SIBLING callback page proves this is a real, known vector and that the login page simply missed it: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/auth/callback/page.tsx:116-125 guards the same class of redirect param with THREE conditions — `rawRedirect.startsWith('/') && !rawRedirect.startsWith('//') && !rawRedirect.startsWith('/\\')` — and its test file callback/page.test.tsx:122-135 has dedicated cases 'rejects a protocol-relative redirect_uri' AND 'rejects a backslash-escaped redirect_uri (`/%5Cevil.example.com`)'. The login page's guard is the same idea with the third (`/\`) clause dropped, and no test exercises the login redirect at all.

Impact: open redirect on the primary email/password login flow across every tenant host. Severity medium (phishing enabler / reputational — requires the victim to follow a crafted link and complete login; no direct data compromise). Confidence high: the full path is traced from the user-controlled `searchParams.get('redirect')` to `router.replace(safe)`, the missing clause is confirmed by direct diff against the tested sibling guard, and reachability is trivial (any anonymous visit to the login URL). Fix: extract the callback's 3-way check into one shared `isSafeInternalRedirect(path)` helper (reject non-`/` prefixes, `//`, and `/\`, and ideally decode-then-recheck) and use it in BOTH login/page.tsx:72 and callback/page.tsx:122-124; add the `/\evil.com` rejection test to the login page mirroring callback/page.test.tsx:129.

The three email/password auth pages do programmatic navigation with the raw, non-locale-aware router from `next/navigation` using unprefixed absolute paths, so the user's active locale (cs/de/en) is dropped on the post-auth hop and next-intl's middleware re-resolves to the DEFAULT locale (sk). register/page.tsx:9,26,81 — `import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'` then `onClick={() => router.push('/auth/login')}` (no `/[locale]` prefix). reset-password/page.tsx:9,18,90 — same import, `router.replace('/auth/login')`. login/page.tsx:20,31,73 — `router.replace(safe)` where `safe` defaults to bare `'/'` when no redirect param is present.

This contradicts the app's own stated locale-routing convention: login/page.tsx:16-24 documents 'Internal links use the locale-aware `Link` from `src/i18n/routing`' and imports `Link` from `@/i18n/routing`, and that locale-aware navigation wrapper is used pervasively across the app (components/ui/Header.tsx, Footer.tsx, LanguageSwitcher.tsx, home/*, etc.). next-intl's createNavigation exports a locale-aware `useRouter`/`redirect`, but these auth pages pulled `useRouter` from `next/navigation` instead — so `Link`s stay in-locale while every programmatic `router.push`/`router.replace` silently falls back to sk.

Impact: a Czech/German/English visitor who registers, resets their password, or logs in without an explicit locale-carrying `redirect` param is bounced onto the Slovak (default-locale) login page or homepage, losing their language mid-flow. Severity low (i18n/UX regression, no data or auth-correctness impact). Confidence medium: the raw-router imports and unprefixed paths are confirmed by static read and contradict the documented convention + the locale-aware wrapper the rest of the app uses; the exact default-locale landing is inferred from next-intl routing behaviour rather than runtime-confirmed. Fix: import `useRouter` (and `redirect`) from the app's `@/i18n/routing` (or `@/i18n/navigation`) locale-aware navigation in all three auth pages so `router.push`/`router.replace` preserve the active locale, matching the `Link` usage already in login/page.tsx.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-06 mobile-rn dashboard layout stale-while-revalidate first-paint gap)
evidence: useDashboardLayout.ts:37-58 -- the Phase-2 'background fetch' does `const fresh = await apiRequest<ResolvedScreen>('/api/v1/layout/resolved/${screen}?platform=mobile')` and, on a valid shape, calls `writeCachedLayout(sid, screen, fresh)` ONLY. It NEVER calls `setLayout(fresh)` (the comment at :37 says 'writes cache ONLY (never sets state)'). The rendered layout is set exclusively by Phase-1 cache-read at mount (:32-35) or the `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_LAYOUT` initial state (:16).

Consequence on FIRST visit for a user/org: Phase-1 `readCachedLayout(sid, screen)` returns null (no cache yet) so `setLayout` is not called and the screen renders `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_LAYOUT`. Phase-2 fetches the org's real server-resolved layout and writes it to cache but does not apply it to state -- so a tenant that has configured a CUSTOM dashboard layout server-side sees the DEFAULT layout on first view and their custom layout only appears the NEXT time the screen mounts. The server-resolved layout is silently ignored on first paint.

Same gap masks server-side CHANGES within a session: after an org admin updates the layout, an existing user renders the STALE cached layout for the whole current mount and the fresh one only takes effect on a later remount -- acceptable as deliberate stale-while-revalidate, but combined with the first-visit-default case above it means a newly provisioned custom layout is effectively invisible until the user navigates away and back.
Reproduce (static): grep -n 'setLayout' frontend/apps/mobile/src/features/layout/useDashboardLayout.ts shows setLayout is called only in Phase-1 (:34), never in the Phase-2 fetch block (:42-52).

Non-duplicate: no prior *mobile-rn*.json signal references features/layout or useDashboardLayout (verified across all 22 mobile-rn signal files; prior layout-adjacent code was never reviewed). Landable remedy (frontend-only, no backend/KMP): in Phase-2, after the shape-check, also `if (!cancelled) setLayout(fresh)` (optionally only when the fetched layout differs from what is displayed) so the server-resolved layout is applied on first visit; keep the cache write for cold-start. Confidence medium: the missing setLayout is code-verified statically; the exact first-paint UX was not runtime-confirmed.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-06 mobile-rn ReportFault caller-side misleading queued-success on permanent 4xx)
evidence: ReportFaultScreen.tsx:312-337 -- the online submit path wraps `apiRequest<CreateFaultResult>('/api/v1/faults', ...)` in try/catch and, in the catch (:327-334), unconditionally calls `queueForLater(payload, t('faults.queuedOnErrorMessage'))` for ANY thrown error. queueForLater (:275-283) enqueues via addToQueue and shows an Alert whose body is the 'saved, will sync later' copy -- i.e. the user is told the fault was saved.

But apiRequest (hooks/useApi.ts:83-92) throws on EVERY non-ok status, so a genuinely PERMANENT 4xx (403 building/permission denied, 409 conflict, 422 server-side validation the client did not pre-catch) also lands in this catch and is queued. On the next processQueue cycle, executeQueuedAction (useOfflineSupport.ts:288-296) classifies any 4xx NOT in RETRYABLE_HTTP_STATUSES={401,408,429} as `permanent`, and processQueue (:422-427) DROPS it with only `console.error('Action permanently failed (4xx), dropping:', action)` -- no user-facing alert. Net effect: the user's fault report is silently and permanently discarded AFTER the UI already promised it was saved and would sync. The idempotency key does not help (the create never succeeded).

The in-code comment at ReportFaultScreen.tsx:328-332 acknowledges 'a genuine 4xx is dropped by the queue' -- confirming the author knew the queue drops it -- but the caller still shows the success/queued message rather than surfacing the validation/permission failure to the user, so the user has no signal their report was rejected.

Reproduce (static): trace ReportFaultScreen.tsx:319 throw -> :333 queueForLater(queuedOnErrorMessage) -> useOfflineSupport.ts:288 isPermanentClientError for 403/409/422 -> :422 drop with console.error only.

Non-duplicate: the only prior queue-4xx finding, code-review-mobile-offline-4xx-drop (2026-07-22), targeted the QUEUE MECHANISM (which statuses to treat as permanent) and its recommended fix -- exclude 401/408/429 -- has since been IMPLEMENTED (RETRYABLE_HTTP_STATUSES). THIS finding is the residual CALLER-side defect: ReportFaultScreen shows a 'saved / will sync' message for statuses the queue still (correctly) drops, so a genuine permission/validation rejection becomes silent data loss with a false-positive success UI. Verified distinct from all *mobile-rn*.json ids. Landable remedy (frontend-only): in ReportFaultScreen's catch, only queue+message when the error is transient/offline (5xx/network); for a permanent 4xx, surface the server error to the user (Alert with the parsed message) instead of the queued-success copy -- optionally have queueForLater consult the same permanent classification. Confidence medium: the code path is statically verified; whether a specific 4xx is emitted by POST /faults in production was not run-confirmed.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-06 mobile-rn deep-link path param URL-decode gap)
evidence: DeepLinkHandler.ts:130-134 -- matchRoute extracts route path parameters by assigning the RAW path segment verbatim: `params[paramName] = pathPart;` with no decodeURIComponent. In contrast, query parameters in parseDeepLink (:80,:88-90) are parsed via `new URLSearchParams(rawQuery)` whose `.forEach` yields ALREADY percent-decoded values. So path params and query params are decoded inconsistently.

Effect: a deep link whose path segment carries a percent-encoded character (e.g. `ppt://announcements/a%2Fb` or an id containing an encoded space/unicode) delivers the still-encoded literal `a%2Fb` to the target screen as `params.id`, which will not match the intended server resource id (the app forwards it to navigation / an api-server GET whose path expects the decoded value). For plain UUID ids this never bites, which is why it is low severity, but it is a latent correctness gap for any non-UUID or human-authored id and an inconsistency with the query-param path.

Additional detail: rawPath is `normalized.split('?')[0]` then `.split('/').filter(Boolean).join('/')` (parseDeepLink :78-79) -- purely structural, no decoding anywhere between normalizeLinkUrl and the param assignment, so the raw octets survive end-to-end into params.
Reproduce (static): grep -n 'decodeURIComponent' frontend/apps/mobile/src/qrcode/DeepLinkHandler.ts returns nothing; the param assignment at :133 uses pathPart directly.

Non-duplicate: prior deep-link findings are code-review-mobile-rn-deeplink-mgr-untested / -untested-qr-deeplink-parsers (test-coverage) and -deeplink-url-listener-leak (2026-08-29, listener lifecycle) -- none concern URL-decoding of path params. Verified across all *mobile-rn*.json. Landable remedy (frontend-only): decode path params at assignment, `params[paramName] = decodeURIComponent(pathPart)` (guarded in try/catch for malformed sequences), matching URLSearchParams' behaviour for query params. Low severity, mechanical. Confidence medium: static-only.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/App.tsx:72 — MfaWrapper.verify() calls raw `fetch('/api/v1/auth/mfa/verify', ...)` with a HARDCODED root-relative path, bypassing the app's configured API base URL. Every other API call in ppt-web routes through a configured base: lib/api.ts:64 `DEFAULT_BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || '/api/v1'` (comment: 'In production VITE_API_URL must be set'), and contexts/AuthContext.tsx:97 `API_BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL ?? ''` for the generated @ppt/api-client. The MFA verify fetch uses NEITHER env var.

Impact: in any deployment where the api-server is served from a different origin than the SPA (VITE_API_URL points at e.g. https://api.example.com/api/v1), the MFA challenge verification request is sent to the SPA's own web origin (`/api/v1/auth/mfa/verify`) instead of the api-server, so it 404s and `response.ok` is false — MfaChallengeProvider treats every correct code as a failure and the user can never clear an MFA-gated mutation. MFA (N9) is a security-critical, user-facing auth path. Works only in same-origin/reverse-proxy deploys, silently breaks on split-origin deploys — a latent config-coupling bug and an inconsistency with the rest of the app.

Confidence medium: the hardcoded relative path is unambiguous on static read; whether it breaks depends on the deployment's VITE_API_URL being cross-origin (runtime/deploy-dependent). Fix: build the URL from the same base the rest of the app uses (VITE_API_URL / getApiClient()), e.g. `fetch(\`${import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || '/api/v1'}/auth/mfa/verify\`, ...)` or route the verify call through getApiClient()/the generated api-client so the Authorization header and base URL come from one source of truth (mirrors the lib/api.ts request interceptor).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/api.ts:321 — `export default getApiClient();` is evaluated eagerly at module import. getApiClient() (lines 273-278) lazily creates `apiInstance` via createAxiosInstance() with NO config, so the default-exported instance has `tokenGetter === undefined` and `onUnauthorizedCallback === undefined`. Later, AuthProvider calls configureApiClient() (AuthContext.tsx:352) which does `apiInstance = createAxiosInstance(config)` (api.ts:299) — a BRAND-NEW AxiosInstance. getApiClient() now returns the configured instance, but the default export still references the original, token-less one.

Consequence: any consumer that does `import api from '../lib/api'` (the natural default import for a file literally named `api`) holds an axios instance whose request interceptor has no token getter (no `Authorization: [Bearer]` header, api.ts:201-206) and whose response interceptor has no 401 handler (no silent refresh, api.ts:219-221). Its requests go out unauthenticated and 401s are never recovered — diverging from every feature hook that correctly uses getApiClient(). The module's own design (AuthContext.tsx:340-344 warns 'getApiClient() falls back to a default instance with no token getter') documents exactly this hazard, then re-introduces it via the eager default export.

Currently LATENT: a repo-wide grep found no default-import consumers of lib/api (all callers use the named getApiClient()), so no live request is affected today — hence severity low (+1). But it is a real foot-gun that will silently break auth the moment any future code adds `import api from './lib/api'`. Confidence medium (static-confirmed divergence; impact gated on a future import). Fix: remove the eager `export default getApiClient();` and either drop the default export or make it a lazy getter/proxy that always resolves the current `apiInstance` (e.g. export a Proxy delegating to getApiClient()), so there is a single configured instance.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-06 ppt-web-core AuthContext session init)
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:423-461 (initializeAuth cold-boot path): when a stored user AND an access token are both present, the code calls setUser(storedUser) and treats the session as authenticated. The inline comment at lines 431-432 claims 'Validate the token is not expired (basic check)' but NO expiry check is performed — the access token's `exp` claim is never inspected. decodeJwtPayload() already exists in this same file (lines 220-233) and is used by deriveActiveRole, so the payload/`exp` is trivially readable without a network round-trip.

Consequence: on a cold boot with an expired-but-present access token, the app immediately renders as authenticated (ProtectedRoute lets the user through, protected screens mount and fire queries). The proactive silent-refresh branch (lines 434-449) is only entered when the access token is ABSENT (`else if (refreshTokenValue)`), so a present-but-expired access token SKIPS the boot-time refresh entirely. Recovery is deferred to the first protected API call returning 401, which then routes through handleUnauthorized (lines 614-622) to attempt a refresh. This produces an avoidable authenticated->401->refresh flicker on every cold boot after the access-token TTL elapses (typical short access-token TTLs make this the common case for returning users).

Landable remedy (frontend-only, no backend/KMP): in the `storedUser && accessToken` branch, decode the access token's `exp` via the existing decodeJwtPayload() and, if expired/near-expiry, fall through to the refreshTokenInternal() branch instead of blindly setUser()-ing; or unconditionally attempt refresh when a refresh token exists. Either fixes the misleading comment and removes the boot flicker. Confidence medium: the missing check and the branch structure are code-verified statically; the exact runtime flicker window depends on the deployed access-token TTL (see docs/api/README.md) which was not executed.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/api.ts:213-256 (response interceptor): on a 401 it invokes onUnauthorizedCallback() (line 219) but then does NOT replay the original request — 401 is not in RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES (line 76), so the retry loop (227-252) is skipped and the request rejects with the transformed ApiError. The wired callback is AuthContext.handleUnauthorized (AuthContext.tsx:614-622), which kicks off a silent refresh via `void refreshToken()` WITHOUT awaiting it (comment at 611-612 confirms this is deliberate: 'invokes this without awaiting it ... recovery happens in the background').

Effect: the request that triggered the 401 always fails at the caller even when a valid refresh token is present. The design relies on 'the query layer's next run' picking up the rotated token, but there is a race: TanStack Query's own retry attempts can fire (and be exhausted) against the still-expired token BEFORE the background refresh completes and writes the new token to storage, surfacing a spurious error to the user. Feature hooks that call the raw axios getApiClient() directly rather than through useQuery (the comment at AuthContext.tsx:339-344 names sentiment and predictive-maintenance as getApiClient() consumers) get a hard one-shot rejection with no refetch semantics to save them.
Distinct from the 2026-09-03 ppt-web-core api.ts findings (eager default-export evaluation; websocket send-envelope), which do not touch 401/refresh semantics.

Landable remedy (frontend-only): make the interceptor await a single de-duplicated refresh on 401 and, on success, replay the original request once with the rotated Authorization header (guard with a per-request __retriedAfterRefresh flag to avoid loops, and skip replay for the refresh endpoint itself). Confidence medium: control flow and the non-awaited refresh are code-verified; the retry-vs-refresh race timing was not executed.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-06 ppt-web-core logout cache purge)
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/queryKeys.ts:354-392 defines AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS, a hand-maintained flat allowlist of query-key roots that AuthContext.logout (AuthContext.tsx:583-585) iterates to removeQueries() on logout. Any tenant-/user-scoped query whose root is NOT in this list survives logout and leaks into the next user's session on a shared workstation — the file's own doc-comment (lines 331-352) flags the financial roots as 'the most sensitive and must never survive logout'.

The pattern has a documented history of silent misses: the comment records that issue #712 replaced an over-aggressive queryClient.clear(), and that PR #2650's fix was INCOMPLETE — the 'notification-triggers' root was missed and leaked until caught later (lines 387-391). There is no compile-time or test-time enforcement that ties a newly-added query-key factory root (queryKeys.* in this file, the @ppt/api-client key factories such as messagingKeys, or ad-hoc `queryKey: ['root', ...]` literals in feature hooks) back to this allowlist, so the next added root will again leak by default.

Static cross-check performed this pass (grep of `all: ['..']` factory roots and ad-hoc `queryKey: ['..']` literals under ppt-web/src/features + hooks, plus messagingKeys.all='messages' in @ppt/api-client) found the CURRENT allowlist complete — this finding is about the fragile un-enforced pattern, not a confirmed live leak.

Landable remedy (frontend-only): add a unit test / lint check that enumerates every query-key factory root (queryKeys object keys + imported @ppt/api-client *Keys.all roots) and asserts each is present in AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS (with an explicit opt-out list for genuinely public/lookup caches), failing CI when a new root is introduced without a purge decision. Low severity today (allowlist currently complete) but high blast-radius on regression (cross-session data leak). Confidence medium: allowlist completeness verified statically, not at runtime.

'' silently pins the vote query to the first building with no building selector — a known ppt-web pattern, note only.

The entire `forms` feature ships with zero localization: none of its five page files (AvailableFormsPage, FormsPage, FillFormPage, CreateFormPage, ViewFormPage) import useTranslation / react-i18next at all. backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler/mod.rs:1049 — inside `send_payment_reminders`, the per-invoice loop resolves recipients with `let user_ids = self.get_unit_resident_user_ids(invoice.unit_id).await?;`. This is inconsistent with the error handling used everywhere else in the same file: the inner notification-send loop (mod.rs:1062-1088) uses `match { Ok(()) => .., Err(e) => { warn!; } }` and never aborts the batch, and the sibling jobs (dispatch_vote_closed_notifications votes.rs:214-245, fire_due_report_schedules mod.rs:1305-1352) all `continue` past a per-item error rather than `?`-aborting. One bad unit's resident lookup should skip that invoice, not the rest.

Impact: LOW / self-healing — invoices already processed earlier in the batch were stamped via `mark_payment_reminder_sent` (mod.rs:1094) so they are not re-sent; invoices after the failing one are simply delayed until the next ~60s tick when the transient error clears. No data loss, no duplicate. It is a robustness/consistency smell: a single unit with (e.g.) an orphaned membership row can repeatedly stall the tail of the reminder batch. Confidence medium: the abort is confirmed by static read; the trigger (a transient/permanent error from get_unit_resident_user_ids) is inferred, not runtime-confirmed. Fix (backend-only): replace the `?` at 1049 with `match { Ok(v) => v, Err(e) => { tracing::warn!(invoice_id=%invoice.id, error=%e, "failed to resolve residents; skipping invoice this tick"); continue; } }` to match the file's prevailing pattern.

Cross-cutting send-then-stamp ordering with no downstream idempotency: the scheduler dispatch jobs send notifications FIRST and stamp the dedup watermark SECOND, so a stamp-write failure after a successful send causes the next ~60s tick to re-send to all recipients. votes.rs:246-285 — `notify_vote_closed(...)` is awaited, then `mark_closed_notified(*vote_id)` is called and, on error, only logs `"next tick may resend"` (votes.rs:278-285).
