The individual notify_* calls carry no idempotency key that would let a repeat delivery be de-duplicated downstream (contrast: CreateFault in voice_commands.rs threads an `idempotency_key`, and the OAuth/notification pipelines elsewhere do dedup). So a resend is a genuine duplicate push/email, not a downstream no-op. For payment reminders this means duplicate dunning emails to residents; for vote-closed it means duplicate result notifications to every participant.

Impact: LOW and narrow — it only triggers when the notification transport succeeds but the immediately-following watermark UPDATE fails (a small DB-failure window), and the behaviour is an explicitly-acknowledged at-least-once tradeoff (in-code comments say "next tick may resend"). Filed as a signal because the mitigation is real and unimplemented: thread a deterministic idempotency key (e.g. notification_type + vote_id/invoice_id + user_id) through notify_* so a resend collapses at the delivery layer, upgrading the pattern from at-least-once to effectively-once. Confidence medium (static; failure path not runtime-forced). No fix asserted beyond the idempotency-key direction; this is a hardening backlog item, not a crash/security bug.

The mobile app has NO live-session access-token refresh. `AuthContext.refreshToken()` (contexts/AuthContext.tsx:174) is only ever invoked from two places, both inside AuthContext itself: the cold-start `initialize()` mount effect (AuthContext.tsx:326) and biometric unlock (AuthContext.tsx:275). Confirmed by grep: no screen or hook consumes `auth.refreshToken`, and there is no `AppState`/foreground listener anywhere under frontend/apps/mobile/src that refreshes on resume.

The live request path never refreshes on 401: `apiRequest()` in hooks/useApi.ts (the fetch helper behind useApiQuery/useApiMutation, and the pattern copied into DocumentUploadScreen.tsx:186 and executeQueuedAction) reads the bearer from SecureStore (useApi.ts:60) and, on a non-ok response, simply `throw new Error(\`HTTP ${response.status}\`)` (useApi.ts:83-92). There is no 401 -> refresh -> replay step (contrast ppt-web's lib/api.ts axios interceptor, which added exactly this single-flight refresh-and-replay). So once the short-lived access token expires while the app is foregrounded (AuthContext calls tokens 'short-lived' and uses a 30s TOKEN_REFRESH_SKEW), every query/mutation 401s; TanStack Query surfaces an error, the user is neither refreshed nor logged out, and requests keep failing until the app is cold-restarted (which re-runs init-refresh).

This also strands the offline queue. useOfflineSupport.executeQueuedAction (hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:253) reads the token fresh from SecureStore but does not refresh it; the retryable-401 fix (RETRYABLE_HTTP_STATUSES incl. 401, useOfflineSupport.ts:34, from backlog item code-review-mobile-rn-offline-401-dropped, done) keeps a 401'd queued write instead of dropping it and comments that it will be '...re-attempted (401 replays with a refreshed token)' (useOfflineSupport.ts:285) — but nothing produces that refreshed token during a live session, so a queued offline write flushed after the access token expired retries forever against the same expired bearer and never lands until a cold restart.

Impact: MEDIUM. No data loss (offline writes are retained, not dropped) and RLS still protects the server, but a foreground session outliving the access-token TTL becomes silently non-functional for all reads/writes and stalls offline sync until the app is killed and relaunched. Confidence MEDIUM: all refreshToken() call sites and the absence of an AppState/401 refresh were confirmed statically; the trigger (access-token TTL < a foreground session, per docs/api/README.md token TTLs) is the normal short-lived-JWT case the ppt-web interceptor was built for, but was not runtime-measured here. Fresh vs backlog: the prior done items patched cold-start restore (code-review-mobile-rn-auth-restore-stale-token) and offline-queue 401 retention (code-review-mobile-rn-offline-401-dropped) but never wired an actual live-session refresh; this is the missing systemic piece. Fix (frontend-only, jest-expo verifiable): add a single-flight refresh-and-retry to apiRequest (and executeQueuedAction) on 401 that calls the AuthContext refresh, mirroring ppt-web's onUnauthorized interceptor, then logs out only when the refresh itself fails.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-10 reality-web listing-detail AdditionalInfo section formats prices with a locally-redefined formatPrice hardcoded to en-US, wrong for every sk/cs/de/pl/hu visitor)
evidence: AdditionalInfo.tsx:8-16 -- the section defines its OWN module-local `formatPrice(price, currency)` that calls `new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', ...)` on BOTH branches (the no-currency fallback at :11 and the currency branch at :12-15). The locale is hardcoded to 'en-US' regardless of the visitor's route locale, so on the public, SEO-indexed listing-detail page a Slovak/Czech/German buyer sees US-formatted money (comma thousands + '.' decimals + '$'-style symbol placement) instead of `1 234 €` / `1.234 €`. This is a customer-facing correctness defect on the money field of the primary listing page.

This directly re-introduces the anti-pattern the codebase's shared helper was built to kill: lib/format.ts header (:1-17) states it 'Replaces scattered Number#toLocaleString(...) / Intl.NumberFormat(\'en-US\', {...}) call sites that all hardcoded a single locale and produced visibly wrong output for the other five', and exposes `formatPrice(value, locale, options)` (lib/format.ts:48-59) that threads bcp47(locale) + defaults to EUR. AdditionalInfo bypasses it with an inline en-US copy.

The locale is trivially available in this component -- it is a `[locale]` route section and already calls `useTranslations('listing')` at :20, so `useLocale()` is in scope. The fix is frontend-only: delete the local formatPrice and import `formatPrice` from '@/lib/format', calling `formatPrice(price, locale, { currency })`.

Reproduce (static): grep -n "'en-US'" components/listings/sections/AdditionalInfo.tsx -> :11 and :12; grep -n 'import.*format' AdditionalInfo.tsx -> no import from lib/format. Contrast ListingCard.tsx:106 which correctly does `formatPrice(listing.price, locale, { currency: listing.currency })`.

Non-duplicate: verified against all 92 prior *reality-web*.json ids -- no prior id references AdditionalInfo or a hardcoded 'en-US' formatter. Distinct from code-review-reality-web-categorycards-tolocalestring-no-locale (that was a bare `toLocaleString()` on a homepage COUNT; this is an explicit `Intl.NumberFormat('en-US')` on a PRICE in the listing-detail section registry) and from the missing-string i18n findings. Confidence medium: the en-US hardcode is code-verified statically; exact rendered glyphs depend on the runtime Intl data, not run-confirmed.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-10 reality-web AgencyDashboard defines a local locale-less formatNumber with hardcoded English K/M magnitude suffixes, shadowing the shared locale-aware helper)
evidence: AgencyDashboard.tsx:889-893 defines a module-local `function formatNumber(num: number): string` that returns `${(num/1000000).toFixed(1)}M` / `${(num/1000).toFixed(1)}K` / `num.toString()`. It (a) hardcodes English magnitude suffixes 'K'/'M' -- a German/Slovak agency owner sees English abbreviations; (b) uses toFixed which forces a '.' decimal separator regardless of locale (de/sk use ','); (c) for values < 1000 emits bare `num.toString()` with no locale grouping. It is used for the stat cards at :402 `value: formatNumber(stats.totalViews)` (called with ONE arg, so it resolves to this local fn, NOT the shared one).

This shadows and contradicts lib/format.ts#formatNumber(value, locale, options) (:38-45), the app's designated locale-aware helper whose header (:1-17) exists precisely to replace 'scattered ... call sites that all hardcoded a single locale'. The shared fn requires a locale arg; the local one takes none, which is why the single-arg call at :402 silently binds to the wrong function.

The component already imports next-intl useTranslations (:17) and is a `[locale]` route, so `useLocale()` is available to thread. Landable remedy (frontend-only): remove the local formatNumber, import formatNumber from '@/lib/format', and either use `formatNumber(value, locale, { notation: 'compact' })` (locale-aware compact 'K/M'/'tis.'/'Mio.') or full locale grouping.

Reproduce (static): sed -n '889,893p' AgencyDashboard.tsx shows the local def; grep -n 'formatNumber' AgencyDashboard.tsx shows the :402 single-arg call and the local def, and NO import from lib/format.

Non-duplicate: verified against all 92 prior *reality-web*.json ids -- none reference AgencyDashboard or a local formatNumber / K-M suffixes. Related theme to the AdditionalInfo en-US finding this same run but a DISTINCT file + distinct mechanism (a redefined abbreviating helper vs an en-US Intl call). Low severity (authenticated agency dashboard, cosmetic). Confidence medium: static-only.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-11 mobile-rn NFCAccessController.addToWallet builds the Apple Wallet pass with a SCRAMBLED reverse-DNS passTypeIdentifier — 'pass.bit.two.three.ppt.access' — that does not match the project namespace three.two.bit.ppt, so it cannot match the Apple Developer Portal pass-type registration / provisioning profile the code's own comment requires)
evidence: NFCAccessController.ts:383 sets `passTypeIdentifier: 'pass.bit.two.three.ppt.access'` when constructing the WalletPass for `addToWallet(credentialId)` (the iOS Apple-Wallet building-access credential path, method at :358-391). The reverse-DNS body is SCRAMBLED: it reads `bit.two.three` where the project's canonical namespace is `three.two.bit`. Per root CLAUDE.md the package namespace is `three.two.bit.ppt` and the iOS bundle is `three.two.bit.ppt.management`; app.config.ts confirms this at :250 (`bundleIdentifier: 'three.two.bit.ppt.management'`) and :318 (`package: 'three.two.bit.ppt.management'`). A correct Wallet pass type identifier would be `pass.three.two.bit.ppt.access` (or `pass.three.two.bit.ppt.management.access`), NOT `pass.bit.two.three.ppt.access`.

Impact: Apple requires the passTypeIdentifier to be pre-registered in the Apple Developer Portal and to match an entitlement in the app's provisioning profile — the code's own comment at :382 says exactly this ('passTypeIdentifier must be configured in Apple Developer Portal and match the provisioning profile. See docs/ios-wallet-setup.md'). Because the string embeds a namespace that does not exist anywhere else in the project, `NativeWallet.addPass(...)` (:390) will fail for every iOS user attempting Add-to-Wallet on a building-access credential — the whole feature is dead on arrival unless someone also mis-registered the same typo in the portal (which would itself violate the reverse-DNS convention). This is a security-adjacent access-control feature (physical building entry via NFC-in-Wallet).

Grep-confirmed uniqueness of the typo: `grep -rn 'bit.two.three|two.three.bit|three.two.bit'` across frontend/apps/mobile shows the scrambled `bit.two.three` ordering appears ONLY at NFCAccessController.ts:383 — every other namespace literal in the app uses the correct `three.two.bit` order (app.config.ts:250/318, usePushNotifications.test.ts:61/67/95 appId 'three.two.bit.ppt.management'). This is an isolated transposition, not a project-wide alternate convention.

Landable frontend-only fix (single string constant, no native prebuild — verified by biome + tsc + jest-expo in CI): change NFCAccessController.ts:383 to `passTypeIdentifier: 'pass.three.two.bit.ppt.access'` (align the reverse-DNS body with app.config.ts bundle namespace), and confirm the same identifier is what docs/ios-wallet-setup.md instructs registering in the Apple Developer Portal. Confidence medium: the namespace mismatch vs the project convention is code-verified and unambiguous statically; the runtime add-to-wallet failure is inferred (the portal/provisioning config is not in the repo and cannot be executed in the cloud runner).

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-11 reality-server portal-listings input validation)
evidence: The portal-owner listing WRITE path validates ONLY its enum-like string fields and leaves every numeric and required-text field unvalidated. `create_listing` (routes/portal_listings.rs:207) calls `validate_enum` for propertyType/transactionType/currency and nothing else; `update_listing` (routes/portal_listings.rs:317) adds `validate_enum("status", ...)` but likewise validates no numeric/text field. `price: Decimal` (CreatePortalListingRequest:106, UpdatePortalListingRequest:126) is passed straight into `create_portal_listing`/`update_portal_listing` (portal_listings.rs:239 / :344) with no lower-bound check, so a negative or zero price is accepted.

There is NO database backstop: migration 00049_create_listings.sql:39 declares `price DECIMAL(15, 2) NOT NULL` with NO CHECK constraint (grep for a `price >= 0` / `CHECK (price` on listings returns nothing; the only price-related CHECK in the tree is 00194's `alert_type` enum). The price-change trigger in 00063_reality_portal_professional.sql:100 even guards `CASE WHEN OLD.price > 0 ... ELSE 0`, implicitly acknowledging non-positive prices can exist. So a portal owner (authenticated PortalPrincipal — realtor / FSBO) can POST /api/v1/my/listings or PATCH /api/v1/my/listings/{id} with `price: -1` (or 0) and it is stored and then rendered on the PUBLIC reality-web portal. The reality-web price-display findings (code-review-reality-web-edit-price-zero #2026-09-06, sell-price-nan) are downstream symptoms of exactly this missing server-side guard — the backend is the correct place to reject it.

The same handler also skips emptiness/length validation on the REQUIRED text fields `title`, `street`, `city`, `postal_code` (all non-Option `String`, portal_listings.rs:104-112) and lower-bound validation on `size_sqm`/`rooms`/`floor`/`total_floors` — a whitespace-only title or a negative `size_sqm` is accepted (and `size_sqm` feeds the €/m² aggregation in routes/price_map.rs:164, `AVG(CASE WHEN size_sqm > 0 THEN price / size_sqm END)`, so a negative size silently drops the listing from the price map rather than erroring).

This is a genuine inconsistency, not a stylistic nit: the sibling public write paths in the SAME server validate their inputs thoroughly — the anonymous inquiry/contact path (handlers/inquiries/mod.rs:156 validate_contact: name 2-100 chars, email format, phone format, message 10-2000 chars) and the article-comment path (routes/articles.rs:450 empty + MAX_COMMENT_BODY_LEN). The portal-listing write path is the outlier that trusts the client.

Impact: MEDIUM. No auth bypass and no crash (Decimal arithmetic tolerates negatives), and ownership/RLS scoping is correct (create/update are gated on portal_owner_id/created_by). But an authenticated portal owner can persist semantically-invalid listing data (negative/zero price, empty title) that is served on the public portal and skews the public price-map aggregation. Confidence MEDIUM: the full path was traced statically (handler -> request struct -> repo call -> DB column) and the absence of a DB CHECK was confirmed against migration 00049; not runtime-exercised. Fresh vs backlog: no prior reality-server finding covers portal-listing input validation (prior ones: categories/suggestions i18n+stubs, slug-is-uuid, sso 401 conflation, mark-read swallow, saved-search/import limits, alert-drainer stub, inquiry-detail, watermark). Fix (reality-server-only, cargo-test verifiable): add a small `validate_listing_fields` guard in portal_listings.rs (reject price <= 0, size_sqm <= 0 when present, rooms/floors < 0, and trim-empty/over-length title/street/city/postal_code) called at the top of both create_listing and update_listing, mirroring InquiriesHandler::validate_contact; optionally also add a `CHECK (price > 0)` in a follow-up migration as defence-in-depth.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-11 reality-web listing-detail ListingHeader formats the PRIMARY headline price with a locally-redefined formatPrice hardcoded to en-US, wrong for every sk/cs/de/pl/hu visitor)
evidence: ListingHeader.tsx:6-16 defines a module-local `formatPrice(price, currency)` that calls `new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', ...)` on BOTH branches (the no-currency fallback at :9 and the currency branch at :11-14). The locale is hardcoded to 'en-US' regardless of the visitor's route locale. This formatter renders the listing-detail HEADLINE price at :50 (`<span className="price">{formatPrice(listing.price, listing.currency)}`) and the price-per-sqm at :54, so on the public, SEO-indexed listing-detail page a Slovak/Czech/German buyer sees US-formatted money (',' thousands, '.' decimals, '$'-style symbol placement) instead of `1 234 €` / `1.234 €`. This is the single most prominent money field on the page.

This is the same anti-pattern already filed for a SIBLING file on 2026-09-10 (code-review-reality-web-additionalinfo-hardcoded-en-us-price, AdditionalInfo.tsx) but ListingHeader.tsx is a DISTINCT, un-flagged file and is higher-impact (H1-adjacent headline price vs a secondary section). lib/format.ts header (:5-6) explicitly states it exists to replace scattered `Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', {...})` sites that 'produced visibly wrong output for the other five' locales, and exposes `formatPrice(value, locale, options)` (:48-59) that threads `bcp47(locale)` + defaults to EUR. ListingHeader bypasses it with an inline en-US copy.

The locale is trivially in scope: ListingHeader is a `[locale]` route section and already calls `useTranslations('listing')` at :19, so `useLocale()` from next-intl is available. Landable frontend-only fix: delete the local formatPrice and `import { formatPrice } from '@/lib/format'`, calling `formatPrice(price, locale, { currency })` (mirror ListingCard.tsx:106 which already does exactly this).

Reproduce (static): grep -n "'en-US'" components/listings/sections/ListingHeader.tsx -> :9 and :11; grep -n "lib/format" ListingHeader.tsx -> no import. Non-duplicate: verified against all 95 prior code-review-reality-web-* ids and the only prior 'ListingHeader' string match is in an unrelated 2026-08-19 mobile-native-kmp signal. Confidence medium: the en-US hardcode is code-verified statically; exact rendered glyphs depend on runtime Intl data, not run-confirmed.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-11 reality-web PhotoGallery never resets selectedIndex when the photos prop changes; a stale index dereferences an out-of-bounds photo -> mainPhoto.url TypeError)
evidence: PhotoGallery.tsx:18 holds `const [selectedIndex, setSelectedIndex] = useState(0)` but NOTHING resets or clamps it when the `photos` prop changes — there is no `useEffect([photos])` and no bounds guard. After the empty-array early return (:54), the code does `const mainPhoto = photos[selectedIndex]` (:89) and immediately dereferences `mainPhoto.url` (:100) and `mainPhoto.caption` (:100). The lightbox path is identical: `photos[selectedIndex].url` (:187) and `photos[selectedIndex].caption` (:190/:194). If a mounted instance ever receives a SHORTER `photos` array while `selectedIndex` points past its new end, `photos[selectedIndex]` is `undefined` and `.url` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` -> the whole client subtree of the listing-detail page crashes.

Trigger condition: the same PhotoGallery React instance is re-rendered with a shorter photos array while selectedIndex > photos.length-1. selectedIndex is advanced by the thumbnail buttons (:130 setSelectedIndex(index), up to 4) and the lightbox arrows / keyboard handlers (:29-33, :169, :215). Because Next.js App Router preserves client-component state across param-only navigations within the SAME dynamic segment, a listing-A(12 photos, user on thumb 5) -> listing-B(2 photos) client transition on `/[locale]/listings/[slug]` would reuse this instance with selectedIndex=4 and photos.length=2 -> crash.

Reachability caveat (why score_delta=1, not 2): a static sweep of the current listing-detail tree found NO in-page slug->slug client navigation today — ListingDetailContent.tsx:38 uses a plain `<a href="/listings">` (full reload) and renders no similar/related ListingCard links, and SearchBar's `router.push('/listings/${slug}')` (SearchBar.tsx:49) lives on index/home pages, not the detail page. So the crash is currently LATENT: the missing bounds guard is real and code-verified, but no live trigger path was confirmed. It becomes an immediate reachable crash the moment a 'similar listings' client `<Link>` (a common, expected addition) is placed on the detail page.

Landable frontend-only fix: clamp on read (`const mainPhoto = photos[Math.min(selectedIndex, photos.length - 1)]`) or reset via `useEffect(() => setSelectedIndex(0), [photos])`, and gate the lightbox derefs the same way. Non-duplicate: verified against all 95 prior code-review-reality-web-* ids; the only prior 'PhotoGallery' mention (2026-08-20 code-review-reality-web-listinggrid-empty-i18n) references it incidentally as a component that DOES use useTranslations, not for this bounds bug.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/organizations/members.rs — the three org-membership mutation handlers (add_organization_member :206, update_organization_member :429, and the delete handler at :717) gate on a single coarse permission flag (`users:create` :275 / `users:update` :499 / `users:delete` :717) plus a role-belongs-to-org check (`r.organization_id == id` :305, `new_role.organization_id != org_id` :531). They are otherwise correctly tenant-scoped. But two standard org-RBAC guardrails are ABSENT.

(1) No privilege-ceiling / anti-escalation check: update_organization_member (:509-539) validates only that `req.role_id` exists and belongs to the org — it never compares the target role's privilege set against the acting admin's own. Any member holding `users:update` can therefore assign ANY role in the org, including one strictly more privileged than their own (e.g. a full owner/admin role), to another member OR to themselves (there is no `target_user_id != admin_user_id` self-guard on the update path, unlike the delete path at :717). If `users:update` is ever granted to a non-owner role, this is an in-org vertical privilege escalation. Fix: require the acting role's permission set to be a superset of the role being granted (grant-only-what-you-hold), and reject self-escalation.

(2) No last-owner protection: neither update_organization_member nor the delete handler checks the remaining owner/admin count before demoting (:576-585) or removing (:717+) a member. Nothing prevents the sole remaining owner from being demoted to a member role or removed, orphaning the organization with no one holding owner-tier permissions (no recoverable admin path). grep for `owner_count`/`last.owner`/`remaining` across members.rs returns 0 hits. Fix: before a demotion or removal that would drop the org's owner-tier membership count to zero, reject with 409 (e.g. LAST_OWNER).

Impact: authorization-completeness / defense-in-depth. Both are model-dependent (severity hinges on whether `users:update` is grantable to non-owner roles in the seeded role catalogue — confirm against the roles seed / role_repo before implementing); filed at MEDIUM confidence because the missing guards are confirmed by static read of the handler but the exploitability of (1) depends on the permission model, and (2) is a clear data-integrity gap regardless. Backend-only fix in members.rs (+ possibly a role_repo helper for privilege comparison and an owner-count query).

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/multi_currency.rs:373-411 — the `Trigger exchange rate fetch from external source` handler is a STUB that reports success as if rates were fetched. Line 397-398 comment: `// In a real implementation, this would call external APIs (ECB, XE) / For now, we just log the attempt`; grep for ECB/XE/reqwest/http_client/fetch_rate/external in the file returns only the comment — there is no rate-provider call. Confidence medium: stub behaviour and the swallow are confirmed by static read; whether any consumer actually relies on last_rate_update for staleness is inferred, not runtime-confirmed.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/features/layout/useDashboardLayout.ts:30-58 — `activate()` has two phases: Phase 1 reads the tenant-scoped AsyncStorage cache and calls `setLayout(cached)` if present; Phase 2 does a live `apiRequest('/api/v1/layout/resolved/{screen}?platform=mobile')` and, per the code's OWN comment at :37 ('background fetch — writes cache ONLY (never sets state)'), only calls `writeCachedLayout(...)` on success — it never calls `setLayout` with the freshly-fetched result.

Consequence: the freshly-resolved layout from the server is never rendered in the CURRENT session — only cached for the NEXT app launch's Phase-1 read. On a user's very first-ever activation of the screen (no cache yet, `cached === null` at :33), `layout` state stays at the hardcoded `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_LAYOUT` (from `../registry`) for the entire session even though Phase 2 successfully fetched and validated the real tenant-customized layout — the user only sees their actual dashboard configuration after force-quitting and reopening the app.

Reachability confirmed: `screens/dashboard/DashboardScreen.tsx:57` calls `useDashboardLayout('ppt/dashboard')` directly — this is the app's home/dashboard screen, so the gap is hit on every fresh install / first login on a device, and after any server-side layout customization change (issue #2486's tenant-scoped caching correctly prevents cross-tenant leakage, but the companion 'don't thrash mid-session' choice went one step too far and also blocks same-session self-updates).

Fix: call `setLayout(fresh)` alongside `writeCachedLayout(sid, screen, fresh)` in Phase 2 (guarded by the existing shape-check and `!cancelled`), so a first-time or post-change fetch is reflected without waiting for the next cold start.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/widgets/WidgetDataProvider.ts:26,354-361 — `apiRequest()` only adds the `Authorization: [Bearer]` header `if (this.authToken)`; `authToken` starts `null` and is set solely via the public `setAuthToken(token)` method (WidgetBridge.ts:40-42 delegates to the same method on its `dataProvider`).

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/settings/WidgetSettingsScreen.tsx:33 — the ONLY place in the app that constructs a `WidgetBridge` (`new WidgetBridge(getApiBaseUrl())`, wrapped in `useMemo`). A repo-wide search (`grep -rn setAuthToken`) shows `setAuthToken` is called for `NFCCredentialManager`/`NFCAccessController` and `FeedbackManager` elsewhere, but NEVER for `WidgetBridge`/`WidgetDataProvider` — no `useAuth()` import, no effect wiring the current session token into `bridge`.

Consequence: every widget the user configures via this screen (`bridge.configureWidget` -> `fetchWidgetData` -> the six `/api/v1/{announcements,votes,faults,notifications,...}` endpoints) is fetched with NO auth header. The endpoints are auth-protected, so each request gets rejected (401 -> `!response.ok` -> throw), caught at WidgetDataProvider.ts:374-379, and silently falls through to empty/placeholder widget data (`return {}` fallback, dev-only console.error at :377). Epic 49 / Story 49.1 (Home Screen Widgets) is therefore non-functional end-to-end for real data — every configured widget always shows zero/empty content — with no error surfaced to the user (`handleToggleWidget` in WidgetSettingsScreen.tsx always shows the success alert 'Widget Added' regardless of whether the initial fetch inside `configureWidget` succeeded).

No test file exists for `widgets/` or `WidgetSettingsScreen` (confirmed via file search), consistent with this gap surviving unnoticed. Fix: call `bridge.setAuthToken(token)` from `WidgetSettingsScreen` (via `useAuth()`) on mount and whenever the token rotates, mirroring the pattern already used for `NFCAccessController`/`FeedbackManager`.

ppt-web has NO global auth boundary: App.tsx mounts <AppRoutes /> directly (App.tsx:274) and authentication is enforced purely per-route by wrapping a page in <ProtectedRoute> (components/ProtectedRoute.tsx:121 redirects unauthenticated users to /login via <Navigate replace/>, and its requiredRoles gate at :128-143 is the only RBAC check). There is no top-level RequireAuth/layout route around the table.

11 feature route-groups register authenticated pages as BARE <Route element={<PageRoute/>}/> with ZERO <ProtectedRoute> wrapper, so an unauthenticated visitor to those paths is NOT redirected to /login (the page component mounts for anonymous users). Confirmed by grep across routes/groups/: financial.tsx (5 routes: /financial, /financial/invoices, /financial/payments, /financial/budgets, /financial/reports — financial.tsx:466-476, imports only `Route`), accounting.tsx (/accounting/invoices, /accounting/payment-matching — accounting.tsx:12-13, imports only `Route`), faults.tsx (5 routes :567-571), disputes.tsx (4 routes :481-484), outages.tsx (4 routes :367-370), community.tsx (6), messaging.tsx (3), neighbors.tsx (3), iot.tsx (6), ai-dashboards.tsx (2), announcements.tsx (4). None of these files contain the string `ProtectedRoute`.

This is INCONSISTENT with the ~10 groups that DO wrap every page in <ProtectedRoute>: buildings.tsx (19), leases.tsx (21), rentals.tsx (15), meters.tsx (13), documents.tsx (16), person-months.tsx (9), reports.tsx (5), voting.tsx (7), notifications.tsx (3), and core.tsx's protected subset (30). The split is arbitrary per-feature, which is exactly how a guard silently gets dropped when a new group file is authored by copying a bare template.

Impact: broken-access-control-in-depth + inconsistent UX. Underlying data is not directly leaked because the api-client calls are org-scoped and the server authenticates every request (the bare wrappers default `orgId = user?.organizationId ?? ''` and gate queries with `enabled: !!orgId`, so anon queries no-op), but anonymous users see the app shell / empty financial+accounting screens instead of a login redirect, and any client-only logic in those pages runs unauthenticated. This is a superset of the already-filed 2026-09-16 core.tsx dashboard-unguarded finding (which covered only /dashboard/*); these 11 feature groups are net-new and un-flagged. Fix: introduce a single auth boundary (wrap <AppRoutes/> children — except the public auth routes — in one <ProtectedRoute>, or a parent layout <Route element={<ProtectedRoute><Outlet/></ProtectedRoute>}>), rather than relying on every group file to remember the wrapper. Confidence medium: the missing guard + redirect semantics are confirmed by static read of ProtectedRoute + the group files, but exact anonymous-render behavior of each page is not runtime-confirmed.

evidence: The financial route wrappers issue TanStack useQuery calls but destructure only `{ data, isLoading }` — they never read `isError`/`error` and never surface a fetch failure to the user. FinancialDashboardPageRoute (financial.tsx:70-84) runs getARAgingReport, getOverdueInvoices and listInvoices; on any of these failing it falls back to zeros (`totals` default :88-94, `invoices = invoicesData?.invoices ?? []` :95) and renders the dashboard with totalOutstanding/totalOverdue = 0 and empty invoice counts — i.e. a FAILED load is indistinguishable from a legitimately-zero financial position. Same pattern in InvoiceManagementPageRoute (:157-167, `data?.invoices ?? []`) and PaymentManagementPageRoute (:265-284, payments/unallocated/invoices all `?? []`).

Contrast the correct pattern in the SAME file: FinancialReportsPageRoute (:401-462) threads `activeQuery.error` into an `error` prop (:458) so the reports page can render an error state. The dashboard/invoice/payment wrappers omit this, so the FinancialDashboardPage / InvoiceManagementPage / PaymentManagementPage components receive no error signal and have no way to show a retry/error affordance.

Impact: on a money-facing dashboard, a transient API failure (or an auth/permission error) renders as EUR 0 balances and 'no invoices/payments' rather than an error — a misleading correctness bug that could lead a manager to believe outstanding/overdue balances are zero. Fix: destructure `isError`/`error` from each useQuery and pass an `error` prop (as FinancialReportsPageRoute already does) so the pages can render an error+retry state instead of silently coercing failures to empty/zero data. Confidence medium: the missing error handling is confirmed by static read; whether the downstream page components have an error-state slot to fill is inferred from FinancialReportsPage's existing `error` prop.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/facilities/pages/FacilitiesPage.tsx:35-41 — the module-local `useIsManager()` hook is a hardcoded placeholder that unconditionally `return true;` (line 40). Its own doc-comment (:15-40) admits it: 'Placeholder: Returns true during development to enable all manager features. Replace with actual role check when AuthContext is implemented for ppt-web.' FacilitiesPage.tsx:46 consumes it (`const isManager = useIsManager()`) and passes it to FacilityList at :116 (`isManager={isManager}`).

The stale 'when AuthContext is implemented' premise is FALSE: AuthContext + useAuth are fully implemented and in use across ppt-web — `export function useAuth()` at frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:742, consumed e.g. by contexts/OrganizationProvider.tsx:6 and App.tsx, and the canonical role helper `isManagerRole(role)` (backed by MANAGER_ROLES) already exists at routes/shared.tsx and is used in App.tsx to gate operator nav. FacilitiesPage simply never got wired to it.

Effect: `isManager=true` for EVERY user (residents included) flows into the UI's manager-only affordances — FacilityList.tsx:82 and :141 render the 'Create facility' button `{isManager && onCreate && ...}`, and FacilityList passes isManager to FacilityCard (:160) whose :151 renders the per-facility 'Edit' control `{isManager && ...}`. So a resident viewing /buildings/:buildingId/facilities sees Create + Edit manager controls. This is the outlier: sibling pages set the flag by route intent (MyBookingsPage.tsx:106 `isManager={false}`, PendingBookingsPage.tsx:117 `isManager={true}`), but FacilitiesPage serves all roles and must derive it from the real user.

Impact: MEDIUM — broken-access-control / authorization-completeness smell in the UI. Bounded to UI exposure (backend RLS still rejects the underlying create/update mutations, so no data breach), hence MEDIUM not HIGH. Fix: replace the placeholder with `const { user } = useAuth(); const isManager = isManagerRole(user?.role);` (import useAuth from '../../../contexts' and isManagerRole from routes/shared), deleting useIsManager. Confidence medium: the hardcoded `return true` and its propagation to Create/Edit gates are confirmed by static read.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/facilities/pages/FacilitiesPage.tsx:63-74 — the `listFacilities` fetch runs in a useEffect; on failure the catch (:68-70) does ONLY `console.error('Failed to fetch facilities:', error)` with no error state, and the finally (:71-73) sets `isLoading=false`. There is no `error` state variable at all (:47-51 declares facilities/total/page/isLoading/filters only), so on a failed load `facilities` stays `[]` and the page renders the normal empty 'no facilities' UI — a load FAILURE is visually indistinguishable from an empty building, with no message and no retry.

This is the outlier within the very same feature folder — every sibling facilities page surfaces load/action errors to the user: EditFacilityPage.tsx sets `setError('Failed to load facility')` (:30) and renders `{error && ...}` (:91); BookFacilityPage.tsx sets error (:35) and renders `{error && ...}` (:131); MyBookingsPage.tsx (:45) and PendingBookingsPage.tsx (:46) raise showToast on 'Failed to load...'. FacilitiesPage — the primary list entry point for the whole facilities feature (Epic 56) — is the one page that silently swallows the load error.

Impact: MEDIUM — unhandled error on a user-facing data path (missing error-state UI / completeness). A transient 500 or network drop presents as 'this building has no facilities', misleading managers and residents. Fix: add an `error` state, set it in the catch, and render an error/retry block (mirroring EditFacilityPage/BookFacilityPage), or migrate the effect to a useQuery with an isError branch. Confidence medium: the swallow + missing error state confirmed by full static read of the file.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/meters/components/ReadingForm.tsx:85-90 — the shared numeric change handler coerces with `type === 'number' ? Number.parseFloat(value) || 0 : value`. Because `Number.parseFloat('')` is NaN and `NaN || 0` is 0, clearing a numeric input (or typing a partial/invalid entry) silently rewrites the field to 0 instead of leaving it empty or flagging validation — the user cannot present an empty numeric field, and a fat-fingered entry becomes a real 0 reading.

For a meter READING form this is a correctness/data-entry hazard: a submitted 0 reading is a valid-looking value that can corrupt consumption deltas, and the `|| 0` masks the difference between 'unset' and 'zero'. The OCR-accept path (handleOcrAccept, :138) sets a real number directly, so this only bites manual entry — but manual entry is the primary path when OCR is disabled or fails (the catch at :113-116 falls back to manual entry).

Impact: LOW — input-coercion correctness on a single form field. Fix: keep the raw string in state and validate/parse on submit (or use `value === '' ? '' : Number.parseFloat(value)` and reject NaN in the existing `errors` validation) rather than collapsing to 0. Confidence medium: the coercion is confirmed by static read; classified LOW as it is a manual-entry edge case guarded by downstream submit validation.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-18 ppt-web-core queryKeys/AuthContext logout purge)
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/queryKeys.ts:354-392 — AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS is the explicit allow-list that logout() iterates (contexts/AuthContext.tsx:624-626: `for (const root of AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS) queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: [root] })`). logout() does NOT call queryClient.clear() (issue #712 replaced clear() with this scoped removal), so ANY authed TanStack Query root not present in this list survives logout and is served to the NEXT user who logs in on the same browser until a refetch — a cross-user tenant-data leak on shared/kiosk workstations, exactly the risk the queryKeys.ts:331-352 doc-comment warns about.

RECURRING BUG — this is the same defect class as two ALREADY-FIXED findings: code-review-ppt-web-core-logout-cache-purge-gap (done; added predictive-maintenance/sentiment/notification-analytics) and code-review-ppt-web-core-logout-purge-notif-triggers (done; added notification-triggers, PR #2650 having been incomplete). Each fix patched only the specific roots then known; NEW routed features have since added query hooks under roots that are STILL missing from the allow-list.

STILL-MISSING roots, each confirmed used by a routed, authed ppt-web page via a @ppt/api-client query hook (grep of frontend/apps/ppt-web/src, non-test): 'disputes' — useDispute/useDisputeTimeline/useDisputeSubmissions/useMediationNotes/useMediationSessions (features/disputes/pages/MediationWorkspacePage.tsx, features/disputes/components/MediationChatThread.tsx, routes/groups/disputes.tsx; api-client all:['disputes'] at packages/api-client/src/disputes/hooks.ts:29) — leaks PRIVATE mediation notes + dispute detail; 'leases' + 'violations' — useLease/useLeases/useExpiringLeases/useViolation (routes/groups/leases.tsx; api-client all:['leases'] leases/hooks.ts:23, all:['violations'] leases/hooks.ts:39) — leaks tenant PII / lease financials; 'iot' — useIotDashboard/useSensorReadings (routes/groups/iot.tsx, features/iot/pages/IotAlertsPage.tsx, features/iot/hooks/useIotWebSocket.ts; api-client all:['iot'] iot/hooks.ts:42); 'my-units' — useMyUnits (features/my-unit/pages/MyUnitPage.tsx, routes/groups/buildings.tsx; api-client all:['my-units'] my-units/hooks.ts:9) — leaks resident's own-unit data; 'templates' — useTemplates (features/document-templates/pages/DocumentTemplatesPage.tsx; api-client all:['templates'] templates/hooks.ts:16).

Impact: HIGH (cross-session tenant/PII data exposure on shared workstations); disputes + leases roots are the most sensitive. Confidence HIGH — full static trace from routed page -> imported @ppt/api-client query hook -> confirmed key-factory root -> confirmed absence from AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS -> logout confirmed to purge only the listed roots (no queryClient.clear()).

Fix (cloud-landable, single-file): (a) immediate — add 'disputes','leases','violations','iot','my-units','templates' to AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS in lib/queryKeys.ts. (b) STRUCTURAL to end the recurrence — stop maintaining a hand-curated allow-list: either derive the purge set from every registered key factory (a single registry of *.all[0] roots across queryKeys + the consumed @ppt/api-client key factories), or invert to a small non-session DENY-list and call queryClient.removeQueries() for everything else, so a newly-added feature root is purged by default instead of leaking until someone remembers to append it.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-18 ppt-web-core lib/api.ts default export)
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/api.ts:370 — `export default getApiClient()` is evaluated at MODULE-LOAD time. getApiClient() (:322-327) lazily creates the singleton via createAxiosInstance() with NO config, so the default-exported instance has tokenGetter=undefined and onUnauthorizedCallback=undefined. configureApiClient() (:347-350) — the only thing that wires getToken + onUnauthorized, called once from contexts/AuthContext.tsx:380 — runs LATER (inside a React effect), and rebinds the module-level `apiInstance` but cannot retroactively fix the value already captured by the default export.

Consequence: any consumer doing `import apiClient from '../lib/api'` (default) gets a client that sends every request WITHOUT an Authorization header and never runs the 401 refresh-and-replay branch — i.e. it silently re-introduces the exact defects already fixed under code-review-ppt-web-core-api-token-provider-unset and -api-onunauthorized-unwired (both done). Currently DORMANT: a grep of frontend/apps/ppt-web/src confirms all production consumers import the NAMED getApiClient()/configureApiClient() (features/predictive-maintenance, features/sentiment, routes/groups/person-months, contexts/AuthContext), so nothing imports the default today — this is a latent footgun, not a live break.

Impact: LOW (latent refactor smell / re-introduction trap on an auth-critical module). Fix (cloud-landable, single-file): remove the eager `export default getApiClient()` at :370 (force callers onto getApiClient() which resolves the configured singleton at call time), or make the default a lazy getter/proxy that reads the current apiInstance rather than snapshotting an unconfigured one at import.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/meters/hooks/useOcrMeterReading.ts:26-51,54-72 — the OCR hooks call the app's OWN api-server endpoints (`POST /api/v1/ai/ocr/meter-reading` :45 and `POST /api/v1/ai/ocr/correction` :59) through a bare `ocrFetch()` (:26 `const response = await fetch(url, options)`) that never attaches an Authorization header. The image request (:44-49) passes only a FormData body with no `headers` at all; the correction request (:59-71) sets only `Content-Type: application/json`. ppt-web authenticates with a localStorage Bearer JWT injected by the axios interceptor / setTokenProvider (contexts/AuthContext.tsx:361-390, lib/api.ts:217-229) — there is no cookie session and no global fetch monkey-patch (confirmed: no window.fetch/globalThis.fetch override in src). So both OCR calls go out UNAUTHENTICATED and will 401, and they also omit the `X-Tenant-ID` tenant header, so even if a request landed it would not be org-scoped. Net effect: Epic-128 OCR meter-reading preview and its correction-feedback training loop are broken against a real backend.

This is inconsistent with every sibling raw-fetch-to-own-API caller in this app, which all attach the Bearer token (and tenant header where relevant): features/notification-analytics/hooks/useNotificationAnalytics.ts:35-41 (`headers.set('Authorization', 'Bearer '+token)`) and features/accounting/api/paymentMatching.ts:64-73 (`headers.Authorization = 'Bearer '+token; headers['X-Tenant-ID'] = org`). Landable frontend-only remedy: route ocrFetch through getApiClient() (lib/api.ts — gains Bearer injection, 401 refresh-and-replay, X-Tenant-ID, and ErrorResponse→ApiError transform for free), or, if the raw multipart fetch must stay, attach `Authorization: [Bearer] ${getToken()}` and `X-Tenant-ID` exactly as paymentMatching.uploadStatement does. Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + a hook test asserting the outbound request carries the auth header.

The sentiment (features/sentiment/hooks/useSentiment.ts:17-21) and predictive-maintenance (features/predictive-maintenance/hooks/usePredictiveMaintenance.ts:8-11) hooks carry explicit doc comments stating that routing through getApiClient() is what applies Bearer injection + 401 handling + retry — useOcrMeterReading is the lone hook that ignores that convention and uses a bare fetch.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/predictive-maintenance/hooks/usePredictiveMaintenance.ts:59-70 — `useNeedingMaintenance(daysAhead = 30)` feeds `daysAhead` into the request URL (:64 `...?days_ahead=${daysAhead}`) but its TanStack Query key is the constant `predictiveKeys.needingMaintenance()` (:61 → :18 `[...all, 'needing-maintenance']`), which does NOT include `daysAhead`. So two callers requesting different horizons (e.g. 30 vs 90 days) collide on one cache entry: the second caller is served the first caller's cached data, and changing the `daysAhead` prop on a mounted component will not trigger a refetch. This contradicts the other two hooks in the same file, which correctly thread their query object into the key: useEquipmentList (:30-31 `predictiveKeys.equipment(query)`) and useMaintenancePredictions (:47-48 `predictiveKeys.predictions(query)`).

Landable frontend-only remedy: parameterize the key — change predictiveKeys.needingMaintenance to `(daysAhead: number) => [...all, 'needing-maintenance', daysAhead]` and pass `daysAhead` at the call site (:61). Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` and a Vitest asserting distinct cache entries per daysAhead.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/iot/hooks/useIotWebSocket.ts:26,84-95 — the IoT sensor WebSocket reconnect loop uses a FIXED 5s interval (`WS_RECONNECT_MS = 5_000` :26) with NO exponential backoff, NO jitter, and NO maximum-attempt cap: `ws.onerror` closes the socket (:84-86), `ws.onclose` unconditionally re-arms `setTimeout(connect, WS_RECONNECT_MS)` (:88-95), and connect() re-reads getToken() each cycle. On a persistent outage — server down, Redis unconfigured, or an expired/revoked token repeatedly rejected at the WS upgrade before AuthContext refreshes — the client hammers `/api/v1/iot/sensors/ws` forever every 5s across every mounted telemetry chart (thundering herd, server-log spam, needless battery/CPU/socket churn).

The app already has the correct pattern in lib/websocket.ts:600-637 (WebSocketService.scheduleReconnect): exponential backoff `min(minDelay * 2**attempts, maxDelay)` with `[0.5,1.0)` jitter and a hard `maxReconnectAttempts` cap that flips shouldReconnect=false and emits `connection:max-retries-exceeded`. Landable frontend-only remedy: give useIotWebSocket the same capped backoff+jitter (track an attempt counter in a ref, compute delay like scheduleReconnect, stop after N attempts). Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + a fake-timer Vitest asserting increasing delays and a cap.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-19 ppt-web-core errorHandler backend-message passthrough)
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/errorHandler.ts:221 (`message: data.message || errorInfo.message`) renders the RAW backend `ErrorResponse.message` verbatim as the user-facing error message for EVERY structured error response, regardless of HTTP status class. There is no status-based scrubbing: a 5xx (INTERNAL_ERROR / SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE) that arrives with a structured body takes the `data.message` branch and shows the backend string directly, instead of falling back to the localized generic `errors.catalogue.INTERNAL_ERROR.message` copy. The file header (lines 6-10) documents this as intentional ("raw backend `message`s are passed through untranslated"), but the design trusts the backend to never place internal detail (SQL text, panic strings, internal identifiers, upstream stack fragments) in `message` on server-class errors — a fragile invariant for an info-disclosure surface.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/errorHandler.ts:194 (`message: error.message || copy.message`) is the same pattern for the plain `Error` branch: an arbitrary thrown JS Error's `.message` (e.g. a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`) is surfaced verbatim to the user rather than the generic localized copy — a UX/quality gap in addition to the info-disclosure angle.

Impact: MEDIUM — information disclosure / poor error UX, gated on the backend actually emitting internal detail in `ErrorResponse.message` for 5xx (or an unhandled JS Error reaching parseApiError). Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the passthrough sinks are confirmed by direct read; NOT confirmed here (no build/test, api-server not compiled in this cloud runner) is whether the Rust api-server already scrubs `message` to a safe string for 5xx. If it does, this is a defense-in-depth gap; if it does not, raw server internals reach the end user's screen.

Fix (cloud-landable, single-file frontend edit): in parseErrorResponse, prefer the localized catalogue copy over `data.message` for server-class statuses (statusCode >= 500) and for unknown/absent error codes — e.g. `const isServerClass = (statusCode ?? 0) >= 500; message: (!isServerClass && data.message) ? data.message : errorInfo.message`. Keep `data.message` for 4xx validation/business errors where it is user-actionable. Apply the same generic-copy fallback to the plain-Error branch (line 194). Verifies cleanly in the cloud runner (single-package ppt-web change, no backend/build coupling); errorHandler.test.ts already exists as the natural home for the new cases.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-19 reality-web comparison share-id url encoding)
evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx:38-43 maps the caller-supplied `sharedIds` (parsed from the ?compare= share-link URL param on the compare page) directly into a request path with NO encoding: `sharedIds.slice(0, 4).map(async (id) => { const response = await fetch(`${getApiBase()}/api/v1/listings/${id}`); ... })`. An `id` value containing `/`, `?`, `#`, or `%` (e.g. a hand-crafted or corrupted shared link such as `?compare=abc%23,../foo,x?limit=999`) changes the effective request target rather than being sent as a single opaque path segment.

This is DISTINCT from the already-filed code-review-reality-web-comparison-fetch-unvalidated-cast (2026-08-18), which concerns the RESPONSE side (`response.json() as Promise<ListingSummary>` cast with no shape validation). This finding is the REQUEST side: the un-encoded interpolation of an attacker-influenceable URL param into the fetch path. The two do not overlap and both live in the same loadSharedListings effect.

Impact: LOW — client-side request-integrity / path-injection on a fetch the visitor makes on their own behalf against the public listings API (bounded: no privilege escalation, and Promise.allSettled already drops failed ids gracefully at ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx:54-66). Worst realistic effect is a malformed request / wrong-endpoint hit or a broken shared-comparison for links whose ids contain reserved characters. Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the raw interpolation is confirmed by direct read; the exact reachable id values depend on the compare page's param parsing (not traced in this pass).

Fix (cloud-landable, single-file frontend edit): wrap the id in encodeURIComponent — `fetch(`${getApiBase()}/api/v1/listings/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`)` — matching standard safe path interpolation. Optionally pre-filter sharedIds to the expected id shape before fetching. Verifies cleanly in the cloud runner (single @ppt/reality-web change, no backend coupling).

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-19 reality-web href url-scheme sink)
evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/listings/sections/Resources.tsx:17 (`href={listing.virtualTourUrl}`) and :39 (`href={listing.floorPlanUrl}`) interpolate agent/agency-authored URL fields straight into an anchor href with NO scheme allow-list. These render on the PUBLIC, SEO-indexed listing detail page. A listing whose virtualTourUrl/floorPlanUrl is set to `javascript:...` (or `data:text/html,...`) becomes a stored-XSS-on-click sink: React 19 does NOT strip `javascript:` hrefs at runtime (it only emits a dev-only warning), so the scheme executes in the visitor's browser on the reality-web origin when they click the 'Virtual tour' / 'Floor plan' link. rel="noopener noreferrer" is present (tabnabbing is covered) but rel does nothing against a `javascript:`-scheme href.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/agency/[slug]/page.tsx:297 (`href={agency.website}`) is the same sink for the agency-controlled `website` field on the public agency profile page — a malicious or compromised agency account can plant a `javascript:` URL that fires for any visitor who clicks the '🌐 Navštíviť web' link.

The codebase already recognises `javascript:` / `data:` URL injection as a threat in the adjacent CSS-vars path: lib/tenant-config.ts:243 `sanitizeCssValue()` denylists `javascript:`, `data:`, `url(`, `expression(` for branding css_vars. That helper is CSS-only; there is NO analogous scheme allow-list applied to anchor hrefs. A grep of frontend/apps/reality-web/src (non-test) confirms no safeUrl/sanitizeUrl/isSafeUrl/href-scheme helper exists.

Impact: MEDIUM — stored XSS but gated on (a) a semi-trusted content author (agent/agency) planting the payload and (b) a victim click. Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the render sinks and the absence of any client-side scheme guard are confirmed by direct read; NOT confirmed is whether the api-server / reality-server validates the URL scheme server-side on write. If the backend already rejects non-http(s) schemes this degrades to a defense-in-depth gap; if it does not, it is a live stored-XSS. Either way the render sink should not trust the field.

Fix (cloud-landable, small frontend-only edit): add a shared `safeExternalHref(url): string | undefined` helper in reality-web/src/lib that returns the URL only when `new URL(url).protocol` is `http:` or `https:` (drop the attribute / render as plain text otherwise), and route listing.virtualTourUrl, listing.floorPlanUrl and agency.website through it. Mirrors the existing sanitizeCssValue defense-in-depth posture. Verifies cleanly in the cloud runner (single-package frontend change, no backend/build coupling).

frontend/apps/admin-web/src/components/ImpersonationWrapper.tsx:73-93 — handleEnd() (the 'Stop impersonation' banner action) fires `await fetch('/api/v1/admin/impersonation/${current.tokenId}', { method: 'DELETE', headers })` but NEVER checks `response.ok`. It then unconditionally runs `clearStored(); setState(null)` in the `finally` block (with a `catch {}` that swallows all errors). The inline comment makes it explicit: 'Clear local state regardless — banner must never get stuck.'

Security impact: if the server-side impersonation-revoke fails (backend 4xx/5xx, network error, or the request is silently rejected), the admin UI clears the local banner and reports impersonation as ENDED while the impersonation token/session may still be LIVE server-side. The operator believes they have dropped the elevated identity but has not — an elevated session leaks past the point the human intended to end it. This trades a real privilege-de-escalation guarantee for a cosmetic 'no stuck banner' UX.

Secondary defect (same call): this DELETE omits `credentials: 'include'`, unlike essentially every other admin fetch in the app (Dashboard.tsx, CapabilitiesAdminPage.tsx, MembershipsPage.tsx, usePrincipalCapabilities.ts all pass `credentials: 'include'`). If the impersonation-end endpoint depends on the session cookie in addition to the Bearer token, the revoke may fail server-side — directly triggering the leak above.

Fix (frontend, cloud-verifiable): check `res.ok`; only `clearStored()/setState(null)` on a confirmed 2xx (or an idempotent 404 = already-ended); on failure surface an error + retry affordance and keep the banner (or hard-logout the admin) rather than optimistically clearing. Add `credentials: 'include'` to match the rest of the app. Confidence medium: the swallow + unconditional finally-clear are confirmed by static read; the exact server-side liveness window depends on backend token invalidation semantics.

admin-web makes ~31 raw `fetch()` calls (grep 'await fetch(' non-test => 31 sites across Dashboard.tsx, CapabilitiesAdminPage.tsx, MembershipsPage.tsx, users.tsx, OrganizationsPage.tsx, TenantLifecyclePage.tsx, LoginPage.tsx, usePrincipalCapabilities.ts, features/layout-editor/api.ts, components/MfaWrapper.tsx, components/ImpersonationWrapper.tsx) that bypass the shared `@ppt/api-client` axios instance. AdminAuthContext.tsx DOES register a token provider (`setTokenProvider(() => sessionTokenStore.get())`) so the typed api-client (used only by features/system-announcements) gets auth + the 401/mfa interceptors — but every raw-fetch page re-implements `const headers = {}; if (token) headers.Authorization = 'Bearer ' + token` by hand and gets NONE of the interceptor behavior.

Consequences of the split transport: (1) no shared 401 handling — admin-web has no refresh flow at all (AdminAuthContext exposes only token/setToken/logout, sessionTokenStore), so on token expiry each raw fetch fails independently with inconsistent UX (some throw, some return [], some return {items:[],total:0}) and no consistent redirect-to-login; (2) auth-header construction is duplicated ~31 times, so a new endpoint can silently ship without the Bearer header or without `credentials:'include'` (see the impersonation-stop finding — that exact omission already happened); (3) response-shape/error normalization is re-invented per call site (Array.isArray(data) ? data : data.items ?? []) with no single ApiError type.

Fix (frontend, cloud-verifiable): route admin fetches through a single thin wrapper (or the existing `@ppt/api-client` instance / a shared `adminRequest<T>()` modeled on features/layout-editor/api.ts's already-good `request<T>()`) that centralizes the Bearer header, `credentials:'include'`, `res.ok` handling, structured error, and a shared 401 → logout/redirect. Low-to-medium: not a live crash, but a systemic consistency + security-footgun surface (0 open findings here today; good time to standardize before it grows).

evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/financial/components/BudgetForm.tsx:127-160 — the editable Budget Categories list renders `categories.map((category, index) => <div key={index} ...>` where each row holds TWO controlled inputs: the name text field (:129-135 value={category.name}) and the amount number field (:140-150 value={category.amount || ''}). The list is dynamically mutable: addCategory (:81-83) appends `{ name: '', amount: 0 }` and removeCategory (:85-87) does `setCategories(categories.filter((_, i) => i !== index))`. BudgetCategory carries no stable id (:47 useState<BudgetCategory[]>), so the array index is the only key.

Using the array index as the React key on a middle-removable list of controlled inputs is the classic index-key data-integrity bug: when a user deletes category N of M, React reconciles by position and reuses the surviving component/DOM instances in place, so every row after the deleted one keeps the PREVIOUS row's input DOM state (typed-but-not-yet-committed text, focus, cursor position) while receiving the next row's props — the visible values shift by one relative to the underlying state array. In a financial budget-entry form this silently misattributes category names and amounts, corrupting the totalBudget reduce (:89) and the submitted payload.

Landable frontend-only remedy: give each category a stable id (e.g. crypto.randomUUID() at addCategory time, mirroring stable-id list patterns elsewhere in the app) and key the row by that id instead of the array index; updateCategory/removeCategory then locate by id. Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + a Vitest that types into row 2, removes row 1, and asserts row 2's values stay with row 2.

46 UI files under frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features hardcode the 'en-US' locale in money/date/number formatters — new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', …), Date.prototype.toLocaleDateString('en-US', …) and toLocaleString('en-US', …) — across the financial, insurance, accounting, facilities and reports features. Representative hits: reports/components/KPICard.tsx:16-25, financial/components/RecentPaymentsList.tsx:32,39, financial/components/BudgetCard.tsx:14, financial/components/ReconciliationTable.tsx:17,24, financial/components/BudgetOverview.tsx:22, financial/components/BudgetForm.tsx:169, insurance/components/PolicyCard.tsx:58, insurance/pages/ClaimDetailPage.tsx:72, accounting/components/AccountingInvoiceList.tsx:79, facilities/components/BookingCard.tsx:38, reports/components/ExecutionHistory.tsx:80 (grep -rn "'en-US'" → 46 files).

The ppt-web app is multi-locale (react-i18next; the Reality side ships sk/cs/de/en and ppt-web's primary audience is Slovak). Hardcoding 'en-US' means every monetary amount and date renders with US grouping/decimal separators and US date order (MM/DD/YYYY) regardless of the user's selected language — a Slovak/Czech/German user sees '1,234.56' and '09/20/2026' instead of '1 234,56' and '20. 9. 2026'.

The defect is worse where the currency is explicitly EUR: reports/components/KPICard.tsx:18 sets `currency: 'EUR'` under locale 'en-US', producing '€1,234.56' (US grouping + leading symbol) instead of the correct sk-SK '1 234,56 €'. So the currency code is right but the formatting locale contradicts it.

These same feature folders already consume react-i18next (useTranslation / i18n.language is imported in sibling files e.g. financial/components/InvoiceDetail.tsx, insurance/components/PolicyForm.tsx), so the locale is available at the call site — the formatters simply ignore it. Landable frontend-only remedy: introduce a shared locale-aware formatter (formatCurrency/formatDate/formatNumber that read i18n.resolvedLanguage) and replace the 'en-US' literals; or pass i18n.language into the existing Intl calls. Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + a Vitest asserting sk-SK grouping/decimal output. Fix can land incrementally per feature; the shared-formatter step is the durable one.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx performs all 6 of its internal navigations with `window.location.href = '/registry/...'` (lines 91, 95, 129, 148, 152, 186) instead of react-router's useNavigate. In a Vite React-Router SPA (30 feature pages use useNavigate) each of these forces a full browser navigation: the entire JS bundle re-downloads and re-parses, all in-memory SPA state and TanStack Query cache are discarded, and the user sees a white-flash reload on every 'view / edit / new' action for pets and vehicles — a needless UX and performance regression versus client-side routing.

(Note: window.location.reload() calls elsewhere e.g. ContentModerationPage:281, AmlDashboardPage:77 are intentional error-recovery buttons, not internal nav, and are out of scope for this finding.)

Landable frontend-only remedy: replace the window.location.href assignments in RegistryPage with a useNavigate() hook and navigate(path); optionally clear the paired ContentModerationPage TODO in the same change. Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + a Vitest/RTL test asserting navigate() is called (no full reload). Low severity — UX/perf regression, not a crash — but pervasive within the registry feature and trivially fixable.
